#144217. Tech Report: Tidal Is the First Streaming Platform to Ban AI Music

Tech Report: Tidal Is the First Streaming Platform to Ban AI Music

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (424 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service.
  • On Tuesday, Tidal announced looks to ban AI music from its platform entirely.
  • This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service. If you own an iPhone and a Mac, you might be tempted by Apple Music; if you have more friends on Spotify, you may feel that's the best platform for you. But if your goal is avoiding AI music as much as humanly possible, there appears to be a upcoming uncontested winner: Tidal.

On Tuesday, Tidal announced looks to ban AI music from its platform entirely. Starting Dec. 9, the firm will begin taking steps to remove music it believes is entirely made with AI. Tidal states it thinks the move “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”.

This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music. Back in July, the company revealed that it would start labeling songs completely made with AI, as well as remove tracks it found to be "fraudulent and deceptive." Other platforms have similar policies, or are rolling out similar features. Apple Music, for example, is working on AI labels for its app, too, and Spotify has pushed back on AI to some degree. However, this most recent move makes Tidal the first music streaming service to outright ban AI-generated music from its catalog.

Robert Anderson, Tidal's Music Lead, posted on X about the change. According to Anderson, Tidal identified 43% of the tracks it received in the last 90 days were AI-generated. Per the company's plan, Tidal will remove 29 million songs by the beginning of 2027, roughly 80,000 to 85,000 removals per day. Some 96% of Tidal's AI-generated songs have zero plays whatsoever.

I wouldn't be surprised to see other music streaming services follow suit, particularly Apple Music. Despite rolling out AI-powered features over the past couple of years, including Apple Music's AI-generated playlists, Apple has taken some stands against AI-generated material in general. The latest Apple TV intro was shot in-camera with practical effects, in an era where the tech giant could have easily generated something with AI. If other companies initiative to follow Tidal's lead here, my money's on Apple being first in line.

In a recent development, however, as it stands, Tidal is the only streaming service that supports this initiative. Soon enough, it'll be the sole music app you can use with near-zero ambiguity that the music you're listening to was at least mostly created by humans. (What a sentence.) Avoiding AI-generated music can be tricky, frustrating, and, frankly, exhausting. If that's crucial to you, Tidal might just be your new pick.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking about is the game's difficulty level. Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that Rockstar's data highlighted that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA 5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in the middle." GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with the franchise's tradition. That stated, players can adjust things like aiming controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or harder. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Design producer Scott Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel "appropriate." “We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he explained. Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much. "There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so big, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that, making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth into as well.” GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. Blade Runner 2099 Revives A Major Element From Philip K. Dick's Original Novel

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (887 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that any fan of "Blade Runner" knows that the source material for the film, Philip K.
  • To be fair, "Blade Runner" retains a surprising amount of Dick's novel, with whole swathes of dialogue making it all the way from the author's page to the screen.
  • Sources indicate that this idea didn't make it to "Blade Runner" in any shape or form, however it does appear (and largely intact, too) in this month's "Blade Runner 2099" sequel series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that any fan of "Blade Runner" knows that the source material for the film, Philip K. Dick's novel "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," didn't exactly make it to the major screen fully intact. As influential and unique as it is, Dick's work proved too unwieldy for filmmakers to adapt wholesale. Instead, Hollywood took Dick's themes and concepts and heavily rewrote his stories for the screen. That trend began with "Blade Runner," as original screenwriter Hampton Fancher took the neo-noir concept from Dick's trippy, weird 1968 novel of a human hunting down illegal androids and pretty much discarded the rest. The relationship between "Androids" and "Blade Runner" can be succinctly summed up by the fact that Fancher and director Ridley Scott didn't use Dick's title for the film, eventually going so far as to borrow the title from a completely different novel by William S. Burroughs.

To be fair, "Blade Runner" retains a surprising amount of Dick's novel, with whole swathes of dialogue making it all the way from the author's page to the screen. Yet numerous other plot elements and characters were either altered or omitted altogether. One element in "Androids" which is very key to Dick's worldbuilding is the concept of Mercerism, a religion in which devotees share a looping, pre-programmed experience via a virtual reality machine called an empathy box.

Sources indicate that this idea didn't make it to "Blade Runner" in any shape or form, however it does appear (and largely intact, too) in this month's "Blade Runner 2099" sequel series. The use of Mercerism in the Prime Video show is a great example of showrunner Silka Luisa and her writers knowing Dick and "Blade Runner" well. In fact, the inclusion of a missing element of Dick's novel in a "Blade Runner" sequel is a bit of a franchise tradition.

In "Blade Runner 2099," it initially seems that Silka Luisa and company have included Mercerism as a little Easter egg, as a couple of animated billboards in Los Angeles advertise it. Yet this isn't a winking reference to Philip K. Dick's novel, but is instead foreshadowing. In Episode 6, entitled "Kill the Killers," Cora (Hunter Schafer) and Olwen (Michelle Yeoh) travel to a hideaway where Cora and her brother grew up. It turns out this hideaway is a defunct Mercer Monastery, a place where those who worship the man could come to and use an empathy box or interact with automated priest-like programs (shades of George Lucas' "THX 1138" there).

Mercerism, as detailed in Dick's "Androids," is a religion based around the idea of increasing empathy, since the future of the novel has become so dystopian and isolating that people need to be reminded to have empathy for others (sound familiar?). This is done through the empathy box, which allows consumers to experience a moment from the life of Wilbur Mercer, apparently some kind of martyr. In the box, Mercer endlessly climbs up a hill while being pelted with rocks, and the "empathy" the user experiences is holding onto sensors which deliver increasingly harsher shocks, sometimes resulting in death.

Industry observers note that the idea was first introduced by Dick in a short story in 1964 entitled "The Little Black Box," and then re-used in "Androids." The ironic twist in "Androids" is that Mercerism is revealed to be a total sham, with the video loop having been shot on a soundstage with an actor. Though this isn't addressed in "2099," the obvious decline in Mercerites and decay of the monastery implies that the religion isn't as popular as it once was.

Even though Mercerism didn't make it into a previous iteration of "Blade Runner," the themes behind it are so integral to the story of "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" and its world that its inclusion feels natural. "Blade Runner 2099" smoothly weaves it into its storyline, using it as an allegory for its doomed principal characters as well as its apocalyptic vision of Earth in general. It's used in the show in much the same way Dick uses it in "Androids," as a satiric commentary on how what was initially intended as an aspirational endeavor has devolved into something more pathetic than never believing in it in the first place.

Ironically, Mercerism is not the first element in "Androids" that was left out of "Blade Runner" but made a return appearance in a sequel story to Ridley Scott's film. In "Androids," the character of John R. Isidore (or J.R. Isidore) was reconceived and rewritten as J.F. Sebastian for "Blade Runner," and he was killed during the events of the film. However, when Dick's friend K.W. Jeter wrote the 1995 novel "Blade Runner 2: The Edge of Human," Jeter brought J.R. Isidore back into the story. It's not entirely clear if Jeter intends his Isidore to be the literal same character, or if he's "borrowing" the character in the same manner as Dick borrowed Mercerism from his short story for "Androids." Either way, it established a neat little tradition for the franchise, in which anything or anyone could come back, and perhaps come back different. For a series infamous for characters not ever fully knowing their true identity and heritage, the tradition feels rather poignant.

"Blade Runner 2099" is now streaming on Prime Video.

  • It has been revealed that situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that yellowjackets, the time-hopping survival drama about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive, is coming to an end. Whether or not it sticks the landing, it's been one helluva ride, and we'll soon have room in the streaming schedule for other other reveals about young people having a pretty rough go of it while just trying to survive.

It has been revealed that situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It quickly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, not just a show about girlfights. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

In a recent development, A bit more grounded...but only at first glance, The Stranded takes place on a Thai island in the midst of a tsunami. The island was formerly home to a prestigious high school, and a bunch of students have snuck back for an ill-timed party on the last day of class. A bad idea, clearly, after the storm hits. Kraam (Papangkorn Lerkchaleampote), one of the few students who actually lives on the island, is trapped there along with a couple dozen classmates. Kraam knows the island, but Anan (Chutavuth Pattarakampol) assumes leadership while other students either take on necessary roles or fall in line. As the miniseries progresses, the fresh social order breaks down, even as the island's mysteries reveal themselves and things get weirder and more complex. Stream The Stranded on Netflix.

It has been revealed that A handful of influencers get invited to a remote island, which is obviously a very good thing to agree to that will not lead to dramatic complications in any way. Behind the neon-lit party vibes, there's a cult at work and some ritualistic shenanigans with deadly consequences. Eden is more concerned with the survival horror than with some of the deeper themes and mysteries of Yellowjackets, but we're still playing with shifting power dynamics in this Spanish import. Stream Welcome to Eden on Netflix.

Industry observers note that the premise of The Leftovers is brilliantly subdued: Around two percent of the world's population disappears without explanation, and it's enough to upend just about everything. Politics have adapted to the latest normal, religions have collapsed and reformed, and families have had to make peace with the inexplicable loss of loved ones. The first season revolves around the Garvey family, led by Kevin (Justin Theroux), a sheriff whose wife (Amy Brenneman) left him to join a cult, while subsequent seasons broaden the scope to bring in other characters in other locations. It's more philosophical than Yellowjackets, and quieter, but the shows share an interest in the lingering effects of trauma, and in the stuff we get up to under threat and in the dark. Stream The Leftovers on HBO Max.

In a recent development, the 100 tells the story of the descendants of refugees of nuclear devastation who return to Earth from their habitat in space to encounter the remnants of humanity who have survived on Earth. Naturally, the first people sent to scope things out are the juvenile delinquents (better them than me), and they discover that three civilizations have risen up in the aftermath of the apocalypse, and they are all pretty scary (including one populated by cannibals, naturally). More sci-fi than horror, but the survivalist themes and mysteries here make it more than a decent match. The show builds an impressive mythology over the course of its run, leading to a conclusion that’s borderline metaphysical. Stream The 100 on Pluto TV or buy it from Prime Video.

Sources indicate that when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

A massive apocalyptic tidal wave strikes during the 10-year reunion of the graduating class of an all-girls high school. The event leaves them all trapped together (a nightmare in any event), and forced to survive while reliving old struggles and dramas. It's Yellowjackets-esque, absolutely, but also Australian and a comedy, which doesn't feel like as much of a stretch as you'd think given the over-the-top nature of that show. Stream Class of '07 on Prime Video.

A remote, charming town with some deep, dark secrets (the biggest of which, and one that it shares with Yellowjackets, is rather strongly hinted in the title), Gannibal stars Yuya Yagira as Daigo Agawa, a police officer from the significant city who takes a job in the super cute (and, of course, remote) village of Kuge following some personal trouble. The perfectly charming Goto family runs the town, more or less, and welcomes Daigo and his family. It's all looking pretty great—until a mysterious man gives Daigo's daughter a severed finger as a gift, and his wife Yuki finds the words "Run Away" scrawled over a door in their new home. Just a couple of reasons why I'm more of a city person. Stream Gannibal on Disney+ and Hulu.

Sources indicate that this latter-day plane crash narrative goes all-in on mystery and philosophy, virtually pioneering the timey-wimey reveal format that makes Yellowjackets so juicy. We kick off with flashbacks that peel back the layers of the various crash survivors before diving headfirst into warm-weather polar bears and mysterious underground bunkers and monsters made of smoke. Whether it's an uncommonly smart network show that rewards careful viewing or a load of nonsense is in the eye of the beholder—but it remains one of the most discussed and debated highlights in TV history. Stream Lost on Disney+ and Hulu.

Kathryn Newton heads this surprisingly smart Lord of the Flies riff about a group of teenagers forced to create their own community after all the adults disappear and a dense new forest crops up around their small enclave, cutting them off from everything and everyone else. This one's about coming of age in a world where the usual rules are no longer in effect, and about how we're quick to reestablish an oppressive social order even when outside forces are no longer at work. Stream The Society on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Julianne Hough and stylist Brad Goreski have fully embraced her 30s with a style evolution they know some fans might not like — and that’s OK.

Recent findings suggest that “I really feel like I’m at this next inflection of my career,” Hough, 38, told Glamour in an interview published on Tuesday, November 24, reacting to backlash over some of her season 35 Dancing With the Stars fashion choices. “When you get into your late 30s, you just don’t give a f*** anymore. You’re like, ‘Who am I? What do I want to wear? What makes me feel incredible?’”.

Hough, who cohosts DWTS with Alfonso Ribeiro, noted that her live-show wardrobe has started to reflect all sides of her personality.

In a recent development, “I’ve gone a little bit more vixen-y this year than I have girl next door because we’re trying to find that character,” she explained. “It’s been very strategic.”.

While Hough has channeled her inner vixen with some of her sexier DWTS picks — like the vintage silver Roberto Cavalli minidress she wore on Mariah Carey Night — some of her more risqué looks have caused a stir among fans, including her beige-colored Valentino leotard under a sheer skirt for the semi-finals.

Sources indicate that “Respectfully who is Julianne’s stylist, and why do they need to be fired,” one social media user wrote over a video of the see-through Valentino look. Other customers echoed the disapproval in the comments sections, calling the sexy number “so awful” and “un tasteful” for a family-friendly show.

Goreski, 49, who has worked with Hough all season on her show-stopping looks, doesn’t mind the backlash, telling Glamour, “Any conversation, good or bad, around fashion is great.”.

He noted, “I think people weighing in — they like the hair but not the dress; they thought it was a bad outfit; they think she should fire me — is totally fine, because we’re really excited by what we’re doing, and we put a lot of thought and energy into it.”.

Industry observers note that the stylist added, “I think Jules ultimately brings the looks to life, and I’m glad that there’s another part of the show that people talk about. Not every person’s going to love every look. I know that from being a stylist for 15 years. And that’s OK.”.

Industry observers note that hough was in complete agreement, adding, “The reason things exist and have charge and stay visible [is] people either love it or hate it. They still want to talk about it.”.

Recent findings suggest that “My aesthetic is very joyful. It’s very optimistic. I love the minimalistic vibe, but I also love glamour,” Goreski stated. “So I wanted to take what she’s known for and put my spin on it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Avatar" fans can thank Eywa, because more sequels are indeed coming.
  • Industry observers note that was the future of a billion dollar franchise like "Avatar" ever in doubt?
  • There's also the fact that director James Cameron, who has spent decades immersed in the world of Pandora, wants to direct other projects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Avatar" fans can thank Eywa, because more sequels are indeed coming. As reported by Collider, Disney's upcoming film release slate includes "Avatar 4" (dated for December 21, 2029) and "Avatar 5" (dated for December 19, 2031). These dates aren't necessarily etched in stone; during the 2010s, the release date for "Avatar: The Way of Water" got pushed back so much that many convinced themselves the movie was never coming out. You simply can't rush the quality that director James Cameron demands of the "Avatar" films. But it's a sign Disney wants the movies out sooner than later.

Industry observers note that was the future of a billion dollar franchise like "Avatar" ever in doubt? Keep in mind, the third movie, 2025's "Avatar: Fire and Ash," was the lowest grossing movie in the series. It still grossed just under $1.5 billion, but that's a notably diminished return next to "The Way of Water," which pulled $2.3 billion internationally. "Fire and Ash" was also, like its predecessors, one of the most expensive movies ever made.

There's also the fact that director James Cameron, who has spent decades immersed in the world of Pandora, wants to direct other projects. Cameron is presently working on "Ghosts of Hiroshima," based on the non-fiction book by author Charles Pellegrino, and he's likewise attached to an adaptation of Joe Abercrombie's dark fantasy book "The Devils.".

Recent findings suggest that cameron, who is 72 years old, is in the stage of his life where he has to balance the films he wants to make against the time he has left, and he knows it. As he told the Empire Film podcast back in May 2026, he wants to make the fourth and fifth "Avatar" films in less time, and for less money, than it took to make "The Way of Water" and "Fire and Ash.".

In a recent development, james Cameron told People in 2023 that "Avatar 4" will feature a six-year time jump. Parts of the film were even shot concurrently with "Fire and Ash" to capture the series' younger actors, like Jack Champion (Spider) and Trinity Bliss (Tuktirey), while they still pass as kids.

The "Avatar" films have strong environmentalist themes; humanity wants to colonize Pandora because, by the 22nd century, Earth is polluted, overpopulated, and seemingly dying. We've only seen small glimpses of that in the previous films. Producer Jon Landau told Syfy back in 2023 that "Avatar 4" will change that:.

Industry observers note that "There's over-population and a depletion of our natural resources that make life harder. But we don't want to paint a bleak picture for where our world is going. The films are also about the idea of that we can change course.".

In a recent development, what about lingering threads on Pandora? "Fire and Ash" ended with the recombinant Colonel Miles Quaritch (Stephen Lang) seemingly plummeting to his death. But one of the most essential rules of fiction is if you don't see a dead body, and sometimes even if you do, don't treat mortal peril as confirmed death.

Quaritch already beat death once, and it feels like he still hasn't quite completed his story yet. Even if Lang/Quaritch does sit "Avatar 4" out, "Fire and Ash" ended with his accomplice Varang (Oona Chaplin) still at large. Varang was easily the breakout character of "Fire and Ash," and I'd be shocked if we don't see her return to attack the Sully family again in movie number four.

"Avatar 4" is right now scheduled for theatrical release on December 21, 2029.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving is officially upon us, and many TV and movie fans are going to be re-watching their favorite festive programming. Whether its Friends' Thanksgiving episodes or a trip to Star's Hallow from Gilmore Girls, there's plenty to chose from. Unfortunately we got some bad news for TV addicts, specifically those with a Netflix subscription. Namely that the streaming platform has cancelled two more reveals after just one season, and they both star major celebrities.

According to recent reports, netflix has a reputation for cancelling demonstrates too soon, and it's not going to shake those allegations anytime soon. Deadline is reporting that the streamer recently dropped Will Ferrell's comedy The Hawk. That's not the only victim, as Netflix has also cancelled Dutch drama Amsterdam Empire, starring Famke Janssen. Fans of those shows are likely starting the Thanksgiving holiday with some disappointment about them not returning for sophomore seasons.

Perhaps this shouldn't be all that surprising. After all, The Hawk suffered from poor reviews upon its release back in July. Still, the show featured some stellar comedic talent, with Will Ferrell joined by legends like Molly Shannon, Fortune Feimster and Chris Parnell. The title role Lonnie "Hawk" Hawkins didn't go down as one of the best Will Ferrell characters, but there were folks who watched the silly golf comedy.

Then there's Amsterdam Empire, which had arguably less hype around it than Ferrell's comedy series. Starring Famke Janssen (Goldeneye, The X-Men movies), the show followed her character Betty Jonkers, a former pop star whose coffee-mogul husband is hiding some shady dealings. The show was shot entirely in Dutch, which is the accomplished actress' first language. Unfortunately the show is now over after just one season, which ended on an exciting cliffhanger. This comes after Janssen was noticeably left out of Avengers: Doomsday, despite so many of her X-Men co-stars reprising their roles in the upcoming Marvel movie.

These two titles join the ranks of many shows that Netflix has dropped way too early, to dismay of fans. Some other titles to have suffered this fate include The OA, which was cancelled after two wild seasons and a huge cliffhanger. Then there was Sense8, which got cancelled but eventually got a movie finale after fans made their voices known. Fans have also been hoping to see more of David Fincher's Mindhunter since the last episode aired back in 2019.

It has been revealed that only time will tell how fans of The Hawk and Amsterdam Empire respond to these two shows being cut off at the knees so early in their life on Netflix. For now, the two shows are presently streaming in their entirety as part of the 2026 movie release list. We'll have to see if Will Ferrell and/or Famke Janssen end up responding to this news, especially since it comes in the midst of the Thanksgiving holiday.

According to recent reports, cupertino is one of those TV indicates that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

In a recent development, the film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

Still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

It’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a major-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

If you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a massive payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

The true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the company lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To Latest Tariffs

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the US government has revealed a upcoming round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • In a recent development, the US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
  • Industry observers note that what does this mean for gaming hardware?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the US government has revealed a upcoming round of tariffs targeting several major countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners. Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face different levies. What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back $508 million in refunds from the US government. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s The new tariffs bypass the Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely mean consumers have to cover the difference. Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia, especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even more. Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

The Best Last-Minute Gifts That Don't Feel Last Minute

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give.
  • Recent findings suggest that with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful.
  • It has been revealed that and focus on presentation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

Recent findings suggest that with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

It has been revealed that and focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

Digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

Recent findings suggest that when time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

It has been revealed that pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

In a recent development, include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Recent findings suggest that sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

Recent findings suggest that spiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Recent findings suggest that mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

According to recent reports, I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

It has been revealed that sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

Industry observers note that flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

It’s still hard to believe that a Nor’easter came in and postponed the parade for the first time in its 100-year history (it has previously been outright canceled), and did so on the actual 100th anniversary. Not even from like, snow. It seems like strong winds made the whole balloon part of the parade impossible. That’s crazy bad luck. However, NBC isn’t sitting on its laurels (and neither is Jimmy Fallon). Here’s what’s happening.

It has been revealed that on Thanksgiving, NBC has opted to just throw on last year’s 99th Annual Macy’s Day Thanksgiving Parade at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones. NBC may have 99 problems, but no parade ain’t one. It’s not a bad idea really. The big balloons, c-list singers, and jazzy dance breaks are usually something most of us have on in the background anyway on this auspicious day. But social media consumers have a way better idea.

Industry observers note that A slew of social media customers think the better play would be to throw on a really old Macy’s Day Parade instead of last year’s. One user on X put it perfectly:.

I don't know who needs to hear this, but there are full length recordings of Macy's Thanksgiving Day parades from the '90s, with all the commercials, on YouTube.

They later joked the lineup from 2003 “looked pretty good.” Another user had a specific year request, too, writing:.

If they were smart they would air one from, like, 1991 in full.

This isn't the first Macy's Day Parade controversy this season. If you'd rather go the nostalgia play, another X user even noted you can throw one of these old episodes on via YouTube, and I thank this individual for that hot tip.

If you’re missing the Macys Thanksgiving Day Parade this morning you can find recordings of pretty much any year you want on YouTube. We pick a year and watch it every year mainly from the 90s before it turned into some weird rap event. 😂This year we are watching 1994.

It seems as if NBC’s strategy is the network doesn't want viewers to notice the parade is old, but there will be moments anyone actually paying attention to the broadcast should notice. I’m not saying that’s the world’s worst strategy given I already established a lot of us watch this while doing other tasks. Still, I think just going full in and putting on an older broadcast would be really fun, and I think would inspire people to pay closer attention and see what cultural references from the time are mentioned and what’s changed in the decades since.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, it’s a great idea, and now I just wish it was happening. Meanwhile, I’m still bummed I’ll have to wait a few more days to see Earl the Squirrel blown up in Epic proportion. Luckily, the Macy’s No-Longer-On-Thanksgiving Day Parade will make its triumphant return to NBC this Saturday. Happy 100th, y’all.

Industry News: Avengers: Secret Wars Setting Confirmed By Marvel, Spoiling Doomsday

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It looks like we're heading to the Marvel Cinematic Universe's version of Battleworld in "Avengers: Secret Wars." The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer promises a major showdown between Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom and a conglomerate of heroes from various timelines.
  • We've known for some time that one of Marvel Comics' greatest modern writers, Jonathan Hickman, is a secret MCU consultant, and that "Avengers: Doomsday" is loosely adapting his "Avengers: Time Runs Out" storyline from 2014.
  • In a recent development, the Marvel Studios president told the outlet, "'Secret Wars' is different than any other movie we've ever made.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looks like we're heading to the Marvel Cinematic Universe's version of Battleworld in "Avengers: Secret Wars." The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer promises a major showdown between Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom and a conglomerate of heroes from various timelines. As it stands, "Doomsday" has a real shot at the biggest box office opening weekend ever, which would bode very well for the second part of Joe and Anthony Russo's upcoming duology, "Avengers: Secret Wars." That sequel is due out on December 17, 2027, and if "Doomsday" does what "Infinity War" did back in 2018, it should have a grand old time at the box office. That is, if Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige doesn't spoil things before then.

We've known for some time that one of Marvel Comics' greatest modern writers, Jonathan Hickman, is a secret MCU consultant, and that "Avengers: Doomsday" is loosely adapting his "Avengers: Time Runs Out" storyline from 2014. That arc serves as a prelude to Hickman's 2015 "Secret Wars" storyline, and together these two runs see the Marvel universe collapse due to "incursions," after which Victor von Doom uses fragments of the shattered multiverse to create a upcoming planet named Battleworld. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Feige basically confirmed that this is the setting for the MCU's version of "Secret Wars," basically spoiling "Doomsday" by strongly hinting how that film ends and where the next one begins.

In a recent development, the Marvel Studios president told the outlet, "'Secret Wars' is different than any other movie we've ever made. Look at the comics. The characters and the settings and the worlds within this singular planet where our movie 'Secret Wars' takes place is the imagination gone wild, which is what's exciting about it." So there you have it. Most fans expected to see Battleworld in "Secret Wars," but now it's as close to official as you can get.

The first "Secret Wars" comic book arc arrived in 1984, with writer Jim Shooter and artists Mike Zeck and Bob Layton delivering a story in which the cosmic entity known as The Beyonder forced various Marvel characters to fight to the death on the planet Battleworld. It seems Marvel Studios will draw from this original run for some aspects of "Avengers: Doomsday" and "Avengers: Secret Wars." But for the most part, Jonathan Hickman's 2015 run serves as the basis for the two movies.

According to recent reports, this second "Secret Wars" arc, illustrated by artist Esad Ribić with cover designs by Alex Ross, and the run that preceded it, "Time Runs Out," are the essential inspiration for "Doomsday" and its sequel. Feige told Entertainment Weekly that "Doomsday" is basically the MCU's version of "Time Runs Out," while the filmmakers described "Secret Wars" as "a little bit of both" that storyline and Hickman's "Secret Wars.".

Asked to comment further, Feige noted, "If you wanted spoilers for 'The Odyssey,' you could go read the book. If you want spoilers for 'Doomsday' and 'Secret Wars,' you can go look at the comics," adding, "It is very much the same thing that we're doing." Clearly, then, Hickman's work is integral to the two upcoming MCU releases, with Feige going on to say that "Secret Wars" is "very much" the "culmination of an incursion, multiversal-collapse event." With that in mind, you can bet the "Doomsday" sequel will play out pretty much entirely on the MCU's version of Battleworld, with the surviving heroes from "Doomsday" taking the fight to its god emperor, Doom, in an attempt to overthrow his regime and restore the multiverse. Whether "Secret Wars" will include Marvel's infamous Spider-Man bathroom scene, however, remains unconfirmed.

None of Kevin Feige's latest revelations should come as a big shock to Marvel fans who've known Marvel Studios has been drawing from Jonathan Hickman's "Secret Wars" run. But this is the closest Feige has come to officially confirming Battleworld as the setting for "Avengers: Secret Wars." The Marvel Studios head didn't use the name "Battleworld," but his comments about a "singular planet" were in response to a question about it.

Otherwise, Feige characterized "Avengers: Doomsday" as "a culmination of what's come before," and "Secret Wars" as "a launching pad for [Marvel Studios'] films in 2028 — the 20th anniversary of the MCU." Clearly, then, whatever happens at the end of "Secret Wars" will set the stage for new characters, timelines, and storylines that will reshape the way the MCU looks going forward.

We know that Marvel Studios is preparing its Jake Schrier-directed X-Men movie, which is set to debut in the wake of "Secret Wars." First, though, Marvel is reworking its cinematic universe with "Doomsday" and "Secret Wars." According to co-director Joe Russo, this simply had to be done with two movies due to it being "such a major storyline." He continued: "Doom as a character needs a lot of space, especially when Robert Downey is playing him. So the scale of the story, the emotional scale of the story is so large that it really needed to be a two-parter.".

Recent findings suggest that whether the second part of that two-parter will actually debut on December 17, 2027, however, remains unclear. Production on "Secret Wars" has been moved to 2027, suggesting a delay might be imminent. For now, we'll have to wait and see how things play out. But regardless of when the movie actually arrives, prepare yourselves for a major screen visit to Battleworld.

The spring Tokyo City region treasure hunt is one of the weekly activities in Forza Horizon 6 Series 7, "City Life." Whenever a fresh hunt begins, a box appears somewhere on the map and, to locate it, the only hints you have are the region's name and a picture. Completing this challenge helps you get closer to claiming the weekly and the Series cars.

If you need help locating the box, here's where to find the "City Life" treasure hunt box in Forza Horizon 6.

Patch (Nov. 26): We've added the Series 7 spring Tokyo City treasure hunt location.

It has been revealed that during this week, you will have the chance to complete the last weekly challenges of the "City Life" playlist. The Series 7 spring treasure hunt is taking place in Tokyo City Region, offering 100,000 credits and three seasonal points as rewards for smashing the treasure box.

We can also identify banners advertising the Horizon Festival in the photo. While there's no visual cue in the photo that lets us quickly identify the location, we know from experience that there are few locations where you drive under a roof in Tokyo City.

You can find the spring Tokyo City treasure box inside a corridor that runs through a building in the southern part of the region. If you have already visited the area, you can simply teleport there by using X/Square on the controller or X on the keyboard. Now, if you're not familiar with the area, you can use the Daikoku Parking Area as a reference point. Look northwest of it, on the mainland, and you will find the dotted line marking the corridor on the map.

Breaking: Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (823 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that one of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16.
  • Recent findings suggest that as detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major refresh for Season 16. As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders to open chests for items. Dying means losing half of the cinders you've collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way since Diablo 4 launched back in 2023. https://www.youtube.com/live/zhsLeug_ooo?si=EeprZXb-pEZ_KRiQ In Season 16, that will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos. Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead, players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly. Those changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a full 5,000 stored up. Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. Alongside its Helltide changes, the season will bring substantial updates to War Plans as well. A new system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. Blizzard additionally confirmed many of the features that were added as part of Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like Stone of Jordan.

Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, it seems the tech giant is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Industry observers note that last Thursday, Nintendo confirmed its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.00, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

According to recent reports, if you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:.

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $20 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original launched all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $49.99.

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails for $69.99 for a physical copy on Switch 2, but Nintendo is selling it for $49 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The organization offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $48.97 before Black Friday.

Sources indicate that nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

It has been revealed that nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in Upcoming York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

In a recent development, yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For most of Survivor 51, I thought the season’s defining trait was going to be its wacky and over the top characters. We had a professional wrestler cutting off his thumb. We had a wannabe quitter scheming to try and be medically evacuated. We had a dude planting a fake idol and then accidentally finding his own fake idol. We had a woman losing her pants, a theater kid repeatedly making vampire analogies. I could go on and on about all the vibrant personalities, but with only two episodes to go in the season, it’s now becoming clear Survivor 51 might be best remembered for something else: producing one of the most dominant winners ever.

There are seven castaways left on Survivor 51, and Sharonda is both the best connected player and the one who seems to be running the entire game. Fans have been all over her as the likely winner of the season for weeks, but this past episode in particular screamed her credentials from a helicopter in Fiji. She was given credit in very specific detail for engineering both of the last two votes, and as viewers, we’ve been told exactly where she stands with all the key players left in the game. I mean seriously, let’s just run down her relationships that have been spelled out explicitly.

In a recent development, she’s in a secret pact with Jelly and Devin as part of the helicopter alliance. As an audience, we have been told about this secret group since the first episode, but the remaining players still have no idea what’s going on. That alliance is clearly the main story of the season, and she is right at the center of it.

It has been revealed that then there’s Cristian, who we have seen Sharonda repeatedly manipulate. First he told her about Carter’s idol, then she lied and convinced him to turn on Maggie. It was only at the end of this past episode, after he watched Carter walk out the door, that he finally realized she’s not his friend. Then there’s Eric, who she straight up said she can get to do whatever she wants. I have to assume he feels the same way since he got no confessionals this week to rebut that.

We saw some tension between her and Mike this week, as she advocated for Carter being eliminated and he advocated for Thien An being eliminated. I bet you can guess who won that big showdown. Carter went home, and Mike ultimately voted with Sharonda, despite the fact that he had a final two alliance with the loveable farmer. Maybe he’ll give us a confessional next week where he explains why he went down that path, but from the perspective of the audience, it looks like she just barrelled over him and got her way.

Industry observers note that ordinarily, when Survivor shows us a player looking this dominant this early in the game, it’s a bad sign. It means everyone else is about to conspire to get them out because they’re such an obvious threat to win the game that they have to be eliminated. Maybe that’s what we’ll see with Sharonda, but I’m not so sure that’s going to happen this season. We’re not getting confessionals from other players about how she needs to be taken out, and there aren’t actually many people left in the game who the edit is telling us can win.

In a recent development, seriously, who else can win this game right now? Jelly is definitely the other most likely contender. She’s gotten a main character edit, and we’ve heard castaways talk about how she’s a threat to win the game, but she got two total confessionals this past episode and players have repeatedly talked about getting her out during their confessionals. Devin still has an outside shot I guess. He’s this season’s leader in confessionals, but the edit has also repeatedly dunked on him for all the mistakes he has made.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

That goes double for Mike. We’ve gotten his perspective pretty consistently, but we’ve also heard a ton from other players about how much they don’t like him. He's possible but very, very unlikely. Eric is a wacky side character who seems like a zero vote finalist. Cristian had two confessionals in the first four episodes combined and Thien An is the most underedited player in the entire season who we’re repeatedly told has no allies. Those are the players who are left.

I’m not saying Sharonda is for sure going to win Survivor 51, but if she does win Survivor 51, she is probably going to be remembered as one of the most dominant winners ever. She hasn’t had a single vote cast against her, and she’s voted correctly in every single tribal council so far, except the one where Linnea went home and multiple advantages were played. I’m not counting the Devin and Jelly vote because she’s the one who told them to play the idol and then told us, as an audience, very explicitly that she only voted against them so the rest of the tribe wouldn’t know she engineered the entire thing.

Recent findings suggest that that's actually a positive for her, as is the fact that she’s formed the best relationships with the largest group of players. She also won an individual immunity idol and has gotten basically zero negative content from the edit. Seriously, what are her bad moments? I'll wait...

According to recent reports, if Sharonda wins, it is going to look dominant, and we’re going to be talking about her in the same way we do Tony, Kim and other legends who gave us a masterclass. There’s still a long way to go, but at this point, I think it’s better than 50-50 it happens.

Industry observers note that one of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6? Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected." Recent findings suggest that one of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?

Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly" considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected.".

Latest Update: How Blade Runner 2099 Took Inspiration From Denis Villeneuve's Legacy Sequel [Exclusive]

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's impossible enough to have to live in the shadow of an unabashed classic of cinema, so just imagine dealing with two of them.
  • In a recent development, for showrunner Silka Luisa, this could've required one of two different approaches: stay suffocatingly faithful to the look and feel and tone of the two films or purposefully set off in the opposite direction.
  • "I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's impossible enough to have to live in the shadow of an unabashed classic of cinema, so just imagine dealing with two of them. There aren't many who would have a bad word to say about Ridley Scott's original "Blade Runner (well, except for those unfortunate critics who dismissed it upon release), but Denis Villeneuve's highly-acclaimed sequel "Blade Runner 2049" ain't too shabby, either. Now, Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099" series has the added responsibility of picking up the story where its beloved predecessors left off ... along with all the pressure that comes with that.

In a recent development, for showrunner Silka Luisa, this could've required one of two different approaches: stay suffocatingly faithful to the look and feel and tone of the two films or purposefully set off in the opposite direction. Well, in this case, how about a secret third option instead? During a recent press junket for "Blade Runner 2099," I spoke with Luisa over Zoom about where this show fits in next to its movie kin and how it finds its own niche amid a much wider world:.

"I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".

In a recent development, impressively, Luisa looked to Villeneuve's 2017 movie to figure out the ideal way to do just that. "What was so fantastic about what Denis did with '2049' was, he didn't just rehash what Ridley had done," the showrunner told me. "He really created his own take on 'Blade Runner' that is very much his aesthetic. But it still felt like an evolution of Ridley's conversation." In effect, the key was to thread that very tricky needle for "2099.".

When it comes to the recent trend of legacy sequels that have dominated the last decade or so of franchise filmmaking, it can certainly feel like we can count the worthwhile ones on just one or two hands. Fortunately, for Silka Luisa and her creative team on "Blade Runner 2099," Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" is basically the poster child for legacy sequels done right. Rather than simply retread all the same ground as before (looking at you, "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens"), "Blade Runner 2049" moved the story forward and took some seriously major risks along the way.

Sources indicate that according to Luisa, this gave her all the permission she needed to follow in its footsteps and take things in bold new directions with her show. "That freed us up in a lot of different ways, because it meant we weren't just beholden to repeating the same thing over and over again," she explains. One massive wrinkle in the Prime Video series is the fact "Blade Runner 2099" takes place after a Replicant uprising has shaken up the status quo, putting humans at the bottom of the food chain for once. It's a strange dynamic that our two main characters Olwen (the Replicant Blade Runner played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (the human posing as a Replicant played by Hunter Schafer) are forced to navigate throughout the season.

According to recent reports, as fans tune in, they can rest assured in the knowledge that the series is taking its cues from one of the most ambitious and boundary-pushing legacy sequels of them all. You could do a lot worse than that. All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are now on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable after that. "Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement." Exoprimal season passes are no longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MEIkK11k09U "While Exoprimal’s early hours of repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun, and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat loop." The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom announced it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at 4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players. 2026 has been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties. Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard promptly lost momentum after its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and Latest World: Aeternum began winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4 is gearing up for the arrival of Season 16, but it won't be leaving its popular previous season behind entirely. As detailed by Blizzard in a breakdown of the upcoming Season of Tyrael's Gambit, much of the previous season, Hell's Legacy, will become a permanent part of Diablo 4 going forward. Season 15 served as celebration of the franchise's history, and added a smorgasbord of items and callbacks to previous Diablo titles, including a storyline revolving around Deckard Cain and the return of enemies and boss encounters from Diablo 2. Most of that is carrying forward, Blizzard noted. Due to "overwhelming requests" from the game's community, Blizzard outlined what all from Hell's Legacy will survive. https://youtu.be/2L55dgNzpQ8?si=S_LjlcZ1XBPZ58Xi Hell's Legacy's capstone dungeons will be added, as will the ability to summon a World Boss version of Diablo and take on the cow god Moopisto. The Prime Evil Council is also becoming permanent, and will work the same way the game's other Lair bosses do, with players needing a specific item to open their reward chest after successfully defeating the encounter. Waking Nightmare dungeons will still be accessible, but only by finding Chronicle of Nightmares dungeon keys. Monsters from previous Diablo games will also have a chance to spawn in The Pit. Those who progressed their secret cow level journey can also rejoice, as the secret cow island and its corresponding waypoint will be staying. Many of Hell's Legacy's best items were upcoming versions of classics from older Diablo games, and those Legacy Uniques will be added permanently as well, including the Annihilus Seal and Hellfire Torch Charm. That's all for now, but Blizzard said more of Hell's Legacy could make a return in the future. "Other popularly requested features are being evaluated for rework and may appear in the future," Blizzard said. Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. In addition to bringing forward much of Hell's Legacy, Tyrael's Gambit will additionally overhaul the game's War Plans system and make its Helltide activity easier. Diablo 4 won't receive new expansions going forward, but it is receiving a new class, the Amazon, next year. Blizzard is also hard at work on Diablo 5. Though it's not slated to arrive until 2029, Blizzard has already revealed three of Diablo 5's playable classes and promised it will launch with more class options than any previous Diablo game.
