When discussing the best Batman, I'm pretty sure many people will say that Michael Keaton is #1, and I'm not going to disagree. Keaton OWNED that role. That stated, is he the most interesting live-action version of the character? I'm going to say no.

In fact, I'm one of those weirdos who will acknowledge that while The Dark Knight is most people's favorite Batman movie, I'm actually of the opinion that Matt Reeves’ The Batman is the best Batman flick. That's all because of Robert Pattinson, who I think is the most fascinating version of Batman yet.

Recent findings suggest that with confirmation that Pattinson is the fresh James Bond, I have a good feeling that he might also be the most interesting version of 007 yet. Here's why.

While many people will likely say that Keaton is the best Batman, I think it's even more likely that most people will say that Sean Connery is the best Bond. Every subsequent Bond actor has unfortunately been judged against Connery, with many people saying that they liked Daniel Craig's bruiser Bond since he was a callback to the tough guy Bond that Connery represented.

Industry observers note that connery is also the reason why some people disregard Roger Moore's Bond, as some people think he verges too far into the silly territory. Personally, of all men who have played Bond, my favorite is Pierce Brosnan, but I respect those who prefer George Lazenby or Timothy Dalton.

That said, I think Robert Pattinson, who I've already gone on record calling my favorite modern actor, will probably provide the most interesting take on the character yet. When trying to envision him as Bond, I think of his roles in Tenet, The Batman, and Primetime, all rolled into one. I see him being a subtler, quieter Bond than others (maybe closest to Dalton), and I'm looking forward to him creating his own version far removed from anything like Connery. Can you tell that I'm excited?

We've had a James Bond who's been Remington Steele, a James Bond who was in The Golden Compass, a James Bond who was Indiana Jones’ dad, and a James Bond who was in Flash Gordon, but we've never had a James Bond who was ALSO Batman, and I just love that this is now going to be a reality.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I know I'm not the only person who's ever wondered who has the better gadgets, or who would win in a fight, and now that same actor is literally going to be both characters. We're undoubtedly going to have people who are going to argue that Pattinson is a great Batman, but a terrible Bond, or a phenomenal Bond, but a terrible Batman.

Or, you'll have people like me who think that Pattinson is an excellent Batman and (hopefully!) an excellent Bond, and I love that we now live in a timeline where this is a thing. Stupendous!

In a recent development, honestly, I feel like the search for the next Bond took FOREVER. In fact, just last year, I wrote about how I thought Aaron Pierre would make for a great Bond. Even though it took seemingly a million years to pick another 007, I feel like the final decision came out of nowhere.

Granted, Pattinson had been in the discussion to play Bond for some time now, but I feel like this reveal came out of the blue (Leave it to me to just learn that Pattinson has been manifesting this role for years).

In a recent development, however, now that Pattinson has been confirmed, I'm actually now EXTREMELY excited for this latest Bond movie. So much so that while I wasn't really interested before, I'm now all in for a new Bond film. So, great decision! Robert Pattinson can do no wrong!

Three Years After His Death, EA Is Using AI To Bring Back A Famed Commentator In FC 27

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (891 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title.
  • Industry observers note that motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that EA Sports FC 27 is adding an AI-generated commentator for the first time in the series' history, with famed British commentator John Motson having his voice synthesized for the football title. Motson, who passed way in 2023, previously provided commentary for EA's FIFA series, appearing in the game's first iteration in 1996 and featuring until 2005. According to the BBC, EA approached Motson's wife and son for permission to regenerate his voice and use his likeness for this year's entry in the series. Both agreed to the idea, but neither party has disclosed how much EA has paid for the use. Fred Motson, John's son, stated that he believed his father would've approved of this use of AI. "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Fred stated. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically, but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects." Peter Caulfield, founder of Save Our Voices Now, which campaigns against this exact use of AI, questions whether a family should be able to provide consent for someone who can no longer give it themselves. "If someone has signed a deal allowing their likeness to be used after they die, I have no concern with that," he explained. "But in life or in death, unless you have specifically agreed to it, AI cloning of any kind should not be allowed. Being a family member shouldn't automatically give you that right either." This isn't newly introduced to video games, either. Epic Games used a similar method to bring back the late James Earl Jones' voice for its Star Wars event in Fortnite, with the actor's estate agreeing to the use. It allowed players to converse with the AI bot while playing, and was very promptly removed after some customers managed to get the bot to spew out racist or vulgar phrases, all delivered with the voice of Jones. It also drew the ire of SAG-AFTRA, which claimed that Epic had violated labor practices. Derek Rae, one of the presently employed commentators on EA Sports FC 27, mentioned he was excited by the inclusion of Motson's voice, and that he didn't believe AI was yet going to replace his own work on the game. When asked whether he would make the same decision to have his work endure for years to come through AI, he replied, "I'm hopefully many years away from having to make a decision like that.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games' UK workforce has voted firmly against unionization the week after the studio's latest game, Grand Theft Auto 6, demolished sales records.
  • It has been revealed that the vote was 25% in favor of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
  • Recent findings suggest that the two-week ballot coincided not just with GTA 6's launch, but with an employment tribunal hearing over the firing of 31 Rockstar workers in 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games' UK workforce has voted firmly against unionization the week after the studio's latest game, Grand Theft Auto 6, demolished sales records.

It has been revealed that the vote was 25% in favor of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. It's a decisive result, especially considering a 93.2% turnout for the vote, with 1,544 employees from Rockstar's offices in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating.

Recent findings suggest that the two-week ballot coincided not just with GTA 6's launch, but with an employment tribunal hearing over the firing of 31 Rockstar workers in 2025. Rockstar argued the workers had leaked company secrets, while the IWGB characterized the action as union-busting. A judgment in the case is pending.

The union can continue to represent individual members, and Rockstar staff remain free to organize over pay, overtime, and other concerns, but Rockstar management will not be formally required to meet or negotiate with union reps.

Rockstar Games head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe remarked in a statement that the organization was "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.".

In a recent development, "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe said. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

In its own statement, the IWGB vowed to fight on. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society - this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for," the union remarked. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quentin Tarantino has returned to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" with "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" (why not read our review of the latest movie here?). But this time, while Tarantino penned the script, he isn't in the director's chair. Instead, he's handed directing duties over to his pal David Fincher (who is ending his exclusive deal with Netflix with the film). Tarantino might not be behind the camera, but he still has a presence in the film, and it echoes something he did in "Hollywood" as well.

Recent findings suggest that early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan. To speed-run us through Charlie's successful career, we're given a little montage of his various roles, and that montage is narrated by none other than Tarantino, whose very recognizable voice provides some humorous details about Charlie's work.

Fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too. He actually wasn't the only narrator, either, because during one scene, Kurt Russell, who plays a stuntman named Randy in that film, also provides a little narration. As for Tarantino, he also voiced some crucial narration during a pivotal scene in "The Hateful Eight.".

Recent findings suggest that in fact, the filmmaker has a history of popping up in his movies, either via a voice cameo or a physical appearance. He has a pretty significant role in "Reservoir Dogs," makes a memorable cameo in "Pulp Fiction," gets to use an abysmal Australian accent in "Django Unchained," has his voice heard during a movie playing in "Inglourious Basterds" (and also plays a corpse in the film), plays a bartender in "Death Proof," portrays one of the members of the Crazy 88 gang in "Kill Bill," and lends his voice to an answering machine in "Jackie Brown.".

So while "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" may not technically be a Quentin Tarantino movie, it still feels like one, right down to the obligatory cameo.

Gemini's Upcoming AI Agent Is Surprisingly Useful (If You Use Google for Everything)

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (841 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What started off as "Spark" is now "Task" in Gemini—not to be confused with Google Tasks, the to-do app.
  • In a recent development, to use Task, open Gemini and create a new chat.
  • In a recent development, of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all notable emails, calendar appointments, and tasks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google loves a rebrand. What started off as "Spark" is now "Task" in Gemini—not to be confused with Google Tasks, the to-do app. Google took its Spark AI agent, which used to live in a separate tab, and integrated it into the Gemini interface. Gemini Task is available globally, and it’s completely free to use for some. That said, some features are limited to the U.S. and, of course, subject to some pretty strict usage limits. While not exactly a replacement for ChatGPT Dots or Meta Muse, you can think of Gemini Task as a controlled version of an AI agent that can do quite a lot in the background.

In a recent development, to use Task, open Gemini and create a new chat. You’ll see a Task tab next to Chat. Switch to it, and start writing your prompt. (You’ll also see some suggested options here.) Type your task or action and press "Send." The feature works best if you’ve already enabled Personal Intelligence on your Google account, and have connected services like Gmail, Google Drive, and Photos as well. You can then tag “@Gmail” to use your Gmail account, or even a third-party connector. Task natively supports automation, so you can say something like, "run this task once every day," and the AI will add it to your Scheduled Tasks section.

In a recent development, of course, I did the thing that every AI demo wants you to do: I asked Gemini to create a daily morning briefing for me, highlighting all notable emails, calendar appointments, and tasks. And, in my experience, it works really well. It reminded me of this article's due date, that I have a couple of pitches in my inbox to review, that a credit card bill is due soon, and that there are some holidays around the corner.

Industry observers note that gemini is very good at retrieving information from emails and taking action. For example, I created an automation that collects all my coffee orders for the month and presents the data in Google Sheets. I then asked Task to create a subscription manager for me. Instead of paying for a third-party app, it took a few minutes to collate the services I pay for into one list. It even accounted for the currency differences (some subscriptions are in USD, some in INR) and gave me a tally in INR, along with things like average monthly cost, and more.

According to recent reports, while Gemini can connect to the open web, it's quite a hostile place right now for an AI bot. Websites are blocking agents from accessing their pages, which hinders their effectiveness. I asked Gemini to create a task that monitors the price of the Sony WH-1000XM5 headphones daily. For this, it asked my permission to spin up a remote browser, and loaded up Amazon, only to be blocked instantly. It did succeed in opening Croma though (a national retailer in India), but it took almost a minute for it to figure out that the price had not dropped below what I asked for. Would it be quicker and less resource-intensive if I did this myself? Yes, but the fact that Gemini can do this every evening like clockwork is the real advantage—as long as the websites comply, that is.

It has been revealed that if you're going to try Task in Gemini for free, there are some limitations you should know about. The free blueprint only lets you run tasks once per day, and you can’t be granular about the exact timing. (Paid Gemini prepares have no such restrictions.) You can only run 10 tasks at the same time, while the limit is 50 tasks for AI Pro consumers. Compute-based usage limits will also apply, based on your plan. The free access is right now live in India, the U.S., Canada, Australia, Japan, and South Korea.

According to recent reports, some features, though, are only for U.S. users. Gemini’s feature that lets you call businesses on your behalf is restricted to the States, as is the ability to forward emails to [email protected] to automatically turn the contents of the email into a task (like adding a college schedule to your calendar). U.S. users can also connect their Google Wallet account to set up payments at supported stores.

According to recent reports, gemini Task is not a proactive agent, nor is it trying to be. You still have to check the work. You have to approve any important steps, and if a website blocks AI models, there’s not a lot Gemini can do about it. For someone like me, who’s all-in on the Google ecosystem, I do see value in Gemini Task. The deep and robust Gmail integration is worth it alone. If you’re on the free initiative, set up a couple of background tasks related to Gmail, Google Drive, or background research that run every morning, and call it a day. And if you’re paying for AI Pro, you can get a lot more done.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history. In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others. However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmTC0m7wQbs Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days. Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety. While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6. Image credit: Getty Images / Craig T Fruchtman.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's a very exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe!
  • For years it seemed like seeing the X-Men and Avengers together was a pipe dream, but Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox opened the door for it to finally happen.
  • Press for the next Avengers movie is underway, with the final Doomsday trailer arriving just days ago.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's a very exciting time in the Marvel Cinematic Universe! We're just weeks away from the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday hitting theaters, which features a thrilling crossover with four teams of superheroes. That includes the Avengers and the OG stars of the X-Men movies teaming up for the first time on the substantial screen. Studio boss Kevin Feige recently referenced comments Hugh Jackman made back in the day about this long-awaited moment, and we tracked down the interview.

For years it seemed like seeing the X-Men and Avengers together was a pipe dream, but Disney's acquisition of 20th Century Fox opened the door for it to finally happen. It turns out that long before joining the MCU in Deadpool & Wolverine, Hugh Jackman had hoped to see these teams together on the big screen. Let's break it all down.

Press for the next Avengers movie is underway, with the final Doomsday trailer arriving just days ago. During a recent interview with Empire, Kevin Feige spoke about bringing the X-Men and the Avengers (plus the New Avengers and Fantastic Four) together for the highly anticipated blockbuster. He referenced the Greatest Showman actor by saying:.

Sources indicate that you see interviews of Hugh Jackman 15, 20 years ago saying, ‘People say it’s impossible, but maybe someday the X-Men and the Avengers can all get together.' It just felt right. It just felt like the fun way to culminate a quarter-century of storytelling.

He's not wrong. The MCU has been going strong since back in 2008, but for years it was noticeably missing beloved Marvel characters like Spider-Man, the Fantastic Four, and the X-Men. The latter had its own series of live-action movies for 19 years, which took place separate from Marvel's shared universe. Those worlds are finally colliding in Avengers: Doomsday, to the joy of fans who have been following the respective properties for well over two decades.

It has been revealed that of course, we had to track down the comments from Jackman that Kevin Feige was referencing to the outlet. They actually date back in 2013.

Hugh Jackman spoke about wanting to see this crossover over a decade ago (2013 to be exact), while promoting his spinoff The Wolverine in an interview with Collider (via YouTube). While Marvel characters were spread across three different studios, the Oscar-nominated actor said the following:.

Sources indicate that I believe, maybe I'm optimistic, I understand the Marvel has The Avengers, they have a lot of major things going on. But at some point, I just find it almost impossible to believe there's not a way to bring Iron Man and all the Avengers characters to Wolverine, the X-Men characters, Spider-Man and somehow get them in together.

Industry observers note that turns out, he was right on the money. Of course, it took some extenuating circumstances to allow for this crossover to finally happen. Namely, Disney acquiring Fox, as well as the studio forming a joint custody agreement with Sony regarding Tom Holland's Spider-Man. It might have taken an additional 10 years, but we're finally getting the chance to see the Avengers and X-Men on the silver screen together this December.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In the same interview, Jackman addressed the legal headache involved in the possible crossover.

I don't see the impediment. I'm like 'OK, you've got three studios. Just split it three ways in terms of costs. And Happy Days, it's all coming together.

In a recent development, doomsday has clearly been a long time coming, which should presumably result in massive box office numbers and (hopefully) positive word of mouth. We'll have to see how it all shakes out, but the hype surrounding the project is VERY high. Unfortunately, Jackman wasn't included in the Doomsday cast announcement. Also--Kevin Feige teased more surprise characters being included, and maybe he'll even surprise us and pop up in The Russo Brothers' movie. Fingers crossed for some unexpected moments.

It has been revealed that our answers will come when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. For now, the Avengers and X-Men movies are all streaming over on Disney+.

GTA 6’s Furry Rescue Mission Is A Little Weird, But The Rewards Are Worth It

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamespot

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game.
  • No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game.
  • Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No matter what you do in GTA 6, it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal. How to find Chase the Fox Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM. Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate. Outrun the cops If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle. Reach the parking garage Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry. Courier the group to safety To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks. Choose your reward Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can stock up on weapons and body armor. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your library before the new one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any time soon. The manufacturer has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms.

In a recent development, this week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. The welcome pack for Firestone is valued at $100, and it includes an exclusive Talia skin, chests, avatars and gems. Latest players must reach stage 15 to claim it.

Next week, you can get Strange Antiquities for free. Run a shop full of occult antiques in the eerie town of Undermere, uncover sinister secrets, help the locals out, and do pet your adorable shop cat.

It has been revealed that we're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic consumers have been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've seen spoilers you people wouldn't believe. This article discusses major plot details from all eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099.".

According to recent reports, what's a worse fate in the world of "Blade Runner," to be human or to be a Replicant? Throughout both films, organics in this post-apocalyptic setting were able to "enjoy" their time at the top of the food chain. That all changes in Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099," the live-action story taking place after the world order has been upended and our supposed underlings have gained all the power for themselves. While Replicants were built to be "more human than human," the subtle differences between the two kinds are all but impossible to detect — on the surface, at least. But, as we know, looks can be deceiving; what's underneath is another matter entirely.

In a recent development, leave it to "Blade Runner 2099" to flip yet another classic franchise staple on its head. Traditionally, the purposefully off-putting questionnaire known as the Voight-Kampff test was meant to detect whether an individual is a Replicant or not. In the sci-fi series, the rise of the Replicants and the 50 years that have passed since "Blade Runner 2049" have introduced even more changes. Enter the Index Test, an inverted form of the established quiz. But rather than differentiate between the two beings, this test is meant to detect whether the subject has developed feelings of empathy towards humans.

According to recent reports, in Episode 5, titled "My Lord," we learn far more about this strange newly introduced setup than the show had previously revealed. All we ever saw was the unusually young human girl administering the test, the odd non sequiturs she posed to (supposed) Replicants like Hunter Schafer's Cora, and the results of whether they passed the baseline or not. But that, too, was only scratching the surface.

In a recent development, of all the differences between humans and Replicants, empathy is the biggest of them all. "Blade Runner 2099" draws fairly stark lines in the sand between the two, with flesh-and-blood people now completely helpless before their bioengineered creations. But despite their physical advantages and killer instincts, Replicants' lack of a childhood means they're deficit in that crucial, compassionate emotion separating humans from all other living things. As we soon learn, however, Replicants can feel these strong feelings ... and actually fear it, too.

Recent findings suggest that this is all summed up in the storyline involving Greta (Katelyn Rose Downey), the young human girl we learn has been sold off into indentured servitude and indoctrinated along with many others into administering Index Tests. Episode 5 peels back all the horrifying layers, showing us Greta's training under awfully unsettling circumstances. First, she's taken through a museum exhibit explaining the purpose and history of the Voight-Kampff test, used by human Blade Runners to hunt Replicants. Now, the upcoming status quo means Replicants use this new Index Test to police their own kind — and, as one instructor explains, prevent any "emotional contagion" crossing over from humans to their Replicant overlords.

Recent findings suggest that it's a fascinating idea with some pretty serious implications for our two main characters. Michelle Yeoh's Olwen is currently undergoing some serious emotional turmoil herself, as her search for the missing Replicant and her secret lover Marek (Johnny Harris) ends in his tragic death. Meanwhile, Cora's own emotional attachments makes it only a matter of time before her human identity is made known. As a result, every time they sit down for the Index Test makes for must-watch TV.

All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are streaming on Prime Video.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I watched my first season of Dancing with the Stars this year, and the journey has definitely been a doozy. After tuning in to the competition show on ABC, I was shaken up by the twists and turns that came, including the power of the fan vote that resulted in both Jenna Dewan and Harry Shum Jr. being eliminated ahead of the finale. It turns out that finalist Connor Wood joked about being portrayed as a villain prior to Ezra Frech's historic win.

In a recent development, there was a ton of discourse about DWTS during its last few episodes, with pro Sharna Burgess slamming how fan votes factor in. Plenty of folks online were mad about Wood staying on, while (what many felt were) superior dancers like Harry and Jenna got eliminated. During an interview with THR prior to the finale, Connor spoke about the fan perception of him, offering:.

The rest of the internet, totally different story right now. We’ve gotten to a point where I have become a bit of a villain for some people.

Obviously, Connor didn't do anything actually villainous, but his getting through to the Dancing with the Stars finale was a shock for many viewers out there, especially when you compared his performances to those of other contestants. His placement seemed to be entirely due to fan votes, since Wood had the lowest scores in the final weeks of the show. Some fans were worried about whether or not underdog Tatyana Ali would stay in the competition, which ended up resulting in Connor becoming the "villain" of the seasons.

Clearly, the fan vote on Dancing with the Stars is notable, but it can also seemingly create more division and drama for those watching the acclaimed reality TV series. Later in the same interview, Wood spoke more about this perception as a contestant, offering:.

According to recent reports, I think that they think that I personally voted their favorite off, and it’s like — I’m aware of my level of dance skill. I have nothing to do with me staying here. That’s just been just the dark side of making it as far as we made it. My understanding is that the more that people go home, the more the fans of those people will go to someone else’s page and villainize those people. That’s sad, and it’s just a testament to how invested people are in this show.

In the end, Connor would end up in third place on Dancing with the Stars Season 35, beating fellow finalists Maura Higgins and Tatyana Ali. I can only imagine how his "villain" persona might have been amplified if he managed to place even better... especially if he ended up beating Ezra as the winner taking home the Mirrorball trophy this season.

In a recent development, ultimately the final two pairs of the season were Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov, as well as Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach. The latter would end up going home with the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy, following a viral final performance where the paralympic athlete's prosthetic leg came off mid-performance. It was a truly epic moment, especially when he managed to overcome it and finish the final dance with his partner.

I thought Ezra was deserving of a win before this final dance, but after seeing the way he overcame and finished the performance, the idea of Connor somehow beating both him and Amber was cringeworthy. In the end that didn't happen, and hopefully Wood can shake off his villain status as more time passes.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Dancing with the Stars is streaming in its entirety for those with a Disney+ subscription as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see what drama comes with the next season of the wildly popular series.

Rockstar Games Has A GTA 6 Hit On Its Hands, But Its Union Vote Is A Loss

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).
  • Roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).
  • According to recent reports, voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6's record-breaking launch, and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions. Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB said it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVyCl_Euhmo The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers. With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

Sorry Jason And Lucia, These 5 GTA 6 Side Characters Steal Every Scene They're In

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Although Jason and Lucia are the stars of Grand Theft Auto 6 and amazing characters in their own right, there are lots of side characters who steal the show whenever they show up.
  • These side characters make the world of GTA 6 feel more fleshed out, lived in, and representative of all different kinds of kooky folk.
  • Brian is the single biggest scene-stealer in GTA 6 for one reason: Stephen freakin’ Root!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Although Jason and Lucia are the stars of Grand Theft Auto 6 and amazing characters in their own right, there are lots of side characters who steal the show whenever they show up. From folks critical to the main story path to weirdos you meet if you take the time to stop and chat with someone on the side of the road, GTA 6 constantly introduces wild, memorable characters almost every hour.

These side characters make the world of GTA 6 feel more fleshed out, lived in, and representative of all different kinds of kooky folk. They’re a substantial part of what makes the game special, and we’re thankful that Rockstar Games took the time to make us care about people other than Jason and Lucia. In particular, these five characters emerged as some of the Polygon staff’s favorites.

Brian is the single biggest scene-stealer in GTA 6 for one reason: Stephen freakin’ Root! For years, Root has been one of Hollywood’s ultimate “Hey, it's that guy” character actors. Now, fresh off an extremely well-deserved Emmy win for his role in Widow’s Bay, he brings the same kinetic, frenetic energy to Brian in GTA 6.

The eternal brilliance of Root’s acting comes from the humanity he injects into every character — often people who would be impossible to believe in lesser hands. Like many of Root’s best roles, Brian is a little too wacky for the real world, but there is a clear and nuanced sense of humanity underneath all of that eccentricity. That ethos is reflected throughout the entirety of Grand Theft Auto, and Brian is the key to selling it from the start. —Ari Notis.

Of all the side characters Rockstar has introduced in GTA 6, Raul Bautista (voiced by Manny Pérez) is my personal favorite. He commands attention — not through loud bravado, but through quiet, seasoned authority. Raul carries himself around with a sun-bleached cool reminiscent of Don Johnson’s Sonny Crockett mixed with the criminal smarts of Robert De Niro’s Nick Wells from The Score. Raul isn’t the sort of guy who needs to announce himself or make a show of what he can do. As a seasoned bank heister who knows Vice City like the back of his hand, Raul operates with understated confidence and stays deliberately out of the spotlight, treating high-stakes scores like a craft rather than a spectacle.

Living on a boat also shows he’s calculated down to his quarters and can pull anchor and disappear on a dime whenever the heat closes in. What makes him especially intriguing is how little we know about his past. Who knows? He could’ve easily crossed paths with Michael Townley and Trevor Philips during their early heisting days — and maybe even learned a thing or two from them. — Ryan Epps.

Midway through GTA 6, just as the heists are heating up, Jason becomes an accidental hip-hop mogul. In a series of missions, Jason is called upon to help promote Real Dimez, an up-and-coming rap duo managed by Only Raw Records. The group immediately steals the show the moment they first appear on screen. Played by real Miami rappers Hood Brat and Krissy Celess, Bae-Luxe and Roxy add some welcome levity to the story as they try to get their major break with a ridiculous single about “booty holes.”.

Recent findings suggest that their missions have Jason doing promo photo shoots, breaking into house parties, and shooting music videos as Real Dimez rise to stardom. In a game that’s almost entirely about complex criminal enterprises, it’s a reprieve to get a side-tale about two musical misfits looking for their moment the old-fashioned way. — Giovanni Colantonio.

Jason’s Key Lento neighbor Shirley is a good, kind soul, if a slightly eccentric one. She has her own way of viewing the world, and while it’s certainly centered around a brand of logic unique to Shirley, it’s not a bad thing. She cares about people as much as she cares about her obnoxiously yappy little dog Arugula, and she’s genuinely hurt by the unnecessarily rude comments from Peggy (of “steal her scooter” fame).

Shirley is basically your odd-but-sweet neighbor who you might dread catching the attention of on your way home, but would never dream of showing that dread or turning down a chance to talk to, if only briefly. Hurting her feelings? Inconceivable. And it’s to GTA 6's credit that it encourages you to meet Shirley halfway and be kind to her without judging her oddities. — Josh Broadwell.

According to recent reports, when I pulled up to my first street race in Vice City, I was not expecting to kick off a whole Fast & Furious-like sidequest in the game. Early on, you meet Yago, a talkative and ambitious racer who just has one problem: he can’t drive very well. Yago takes an instant liking to Jason, who guides him through being a better street racer and drug dealer. What ensues is one of the best male friendships in the game — and one that you can entirely miss.

Recent findings suggest that yago and Jason’s dynamic is equal parts hilarious and endearing, as Yago constantly teeters on annoying but is so gung-ho and into Jason that you can’t help but love him. He also exposes a softer side of Jason that you otherwise only see through his interactions with Lucia. I won’t spoil how Yago’s sidequests ultimately play out, but that event ultimately recontextualizes his entire relationship with Jason and ends up making him one of the game’s more nuanced characters. — Tomas Franzese.

If you haven't been paying attention, major retailers have already revealed their prepares and started churning out deals. But you're still in time to make this Black Friday sale a great one. Here's everything you need to know about the big sale.

Black Friday is always the day after Thanksgiving. This year, Black Friday starts at midnight on Nov. 27. Cyber Monday is the Monday following Black Friday, which starts at midnight on Nov. 30.

The major retailers running sales are the usual ones: Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Home Depot, and many others. Currently, Walmart has publicized its aims already and has early deals available. Amazon Black Friday: November 19.

Best Buy Black Friday: November 19.

Walmart Black Friday: November 23.

Target Black Friday: November 27.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Recent findings suggest that unlike Spring or Summer sales, Black Friday doesn't focus on specific categories, which means everything is fair game for discounts. This is one of the best times to make a list of what you need. You're likely to find what you're looking for discounted, and probably at its lowest price it has ever been. Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

According to recent reports, nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. It has been revealed that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

#144173. Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (870 w)

Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (870 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a major enough challenge.
  • It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget.
  • As such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in fresh directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a major enough challenge. Doing so on the small screen adds an extra element of difficulty. Incredibly, "Blade Runner 2099" has overcome the odds to deliver yet another intoxicating excursion into the techno-industrial urban decay-scape so magically realized back in 1982's "Blade Runner" and so faithfully recreated in 2017's "Blade Runner 2049." As such, the Blade Runner franchise is now surely the most consistent on-screen sci-fi saga ever made. (Setting aside sci-fi sagas that are directed by the same person the whole time, like James Cameron's "Avatar.").

It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget. Yet director Ridley Scott and his production team managed to create one of the most believable and immersive worlds in cinema history. The famous "Hades" opening shot immediately plunges you into a future post-ecological collapse, in which technology seems to have almost grown on the wreckage of a fallen world like moss on fallen trees. The debris of society is adorned with neon and machinery, creating an environment in which past and future collide. "Blade Runner" might have been buried at the box office by "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial," but it was an absolutely enthralling sci-fi adventure that came to define the genre.

As such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in fresh directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle. The "Dune" director's take on the world first introduced to audiences in 1982 was immediately familiar as the same one in which Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard did battle with Rutger Hauer's Roy Batty and his band of rogue Replicants. Yet it also felt appropriately evolved for the three-decade time jump. Surely "Blade Runner 2099" couldn't pull off the same trick — especially across eight episodes? Well, it has.

/Film's Bill Bria has hailed "Blade Runner 2099" as the best sci-fi show in years, and it's hard to disagree based solely on the production design. From the moment the show begins, we're immersed in the same world to which Ridley Scott introduced us back in 1982. In fact, "2099" recreates the "Hades" sequence so faithfully you'd think you were watching the original. It's a clever move, too. As the camera slow-zooms on the Tyrell Corporation building and evokes the tone and feel of Scott's film, it establishes "2099" as very much belonging to the "Blade Runner" legacy. But we soon discover that this is not Rick Deckard's future.

Industry observers note that 80 years after Harrison Ford's Blade Runner absconded with Rachael (Sean Young), Replicants have now overthrown their human masters to become the dominant race. It's a major change that refreshes the franchise and helps make it more relevant than it's ever been at a time when the looming AI garbage future has prompted widespread talk of machines taking our jobs.

According to recent reports, as such, it's more important than ever to maintain a tone and design language that's consistent with what came before, so as to reassure fans of the saga that this isn't some sort of wholesale reinvention of the franchise they love, but an evolution that plays out in the same world. "Blade Runner 2099" impressively pulls that off with its opening scene, and it only gets better from there.

It has been revealed that when it comes to the world of "Blade Runner," fans know the deal: Retro futurism and cyberpunk aesthetics meet noirish expressionism in a technological nightmare future. Many franchises have tried to emulate the aesthetic to varying degrees of success, but there is only one "Blade Runner." As Christopher Nolan once told the Directors Guild of America while discussing Ridley Scott's film, it conjures "that feeling that there was this whole world outside the frame of the scene. You really felt there were things going on outside of those rooms where you've seen the film take place.".

"Blade Runner 2099" has somehow managed to make every one of its scenes feel like they belong in that same world. With that in mind, it's truly remarkable how consistent the Blade Runner universe has remained across almost a half-century's worth of projects, each of which has been separated by many years. Even the best sci-fi franchises struggle to pull off what is, admittedly, an almost impossible trick.

The "Terminator" movies have never been able to recapture the intoxicating, doom-laden sci-fi slasher tone that made the first two films so memorable. The "Alien" franchise, meanwhile, has made a point of switching up its style and tone with each successive film — though more recent projects have tried to evoke the feeling of the 1979 original. "Blade Runner" films, however, all feel part of a cohesive whole that gives the entire saga this uncanny sense of existing in a real alternate timeline somewhere — as if we're witnessing an epic, decades-spanning dream play out in the mind of a dying Replicant. Regardless of how you feel about "2099" as a whole, its visual and tonal achievements simply can't be denied.

"Blade Runner 2099" Season 1 is now streaming on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, with plenty of comedy on the 2026 Netflix streaming schedule, I've always appreciated how John Mulaney can take something ordinary and turn it into an absurdly funny story. Whether he's talking about taking his Korean in-laws to CVS, his children saying scary things, or any number of his hilarious stand-up jokes, his delivery makes even the most ridiculous observations sound perfectly reasonable. Although apparently, one fast-food joke didn't survive the trip from the comedy club to one of his specials, and the reason is pretty hilarious.

The story comes courtesy of filmmaker Cairo Smith, who shared an anecdote on X about attending an early test performance of one of Mulaney's stand-up specials. According to Smith, the comedian had been working on a bit about Yoshinoya Beef Bowl, the Japanese fast-food chain known for its rice bowls. Smith writes in his post, as you can see below, that when the comedian asked audiences who'd been to the establishment, a shocking number had, derailing the entire premise.

One time I went to see an early test performance of a John Mulaney special at a comedy club in LA. And he had a joke about Yoshinoya beef bowl where the joke was that nobody goes there. So he asked the audience, like, who here has actually been to Yoshinoya Beef Bowl? And like a shocking amount of people raised their hands and cheered, like so many that he didn't even know how to continue the bit and just moved on. And then when the special came out, pretty much everything was the same but the Yoshinoya beef bowl bit was gone. And now for some reason that's one of the only John Mulaney bits I can remember.November 24, 2026.

According to Smith, the response left Mulaney unsure how to continue, so he simply moved on to his next bit. I have to assume that's not how the comedian was expecting things to god own.

When the finished special eventually premiered, Smith noticed that the Yoshinoya material had disappeared, even though it was the only bit of material they could remember. Considering how many great John Mulaney comedy specials we've gotten over the years, I can't help wondering how many other jokes disappeared during those early performances.

According to recent reports, I think the audience unintentionally created a funnier moment than whatever Mulaney originally had planned. There's something wonderful about a comedian confidently walking into a punchline only to discover that everybody in the room has apparently been eating at the restaurant he's mocking. And it seems Mulaney remembers the experience.

Responding to the story on X, Mulaney acknowledged the memory and revealed that he'd encountered a similar problem while testing a recent joke, writing:.

l remember this well. The same thing happened in September with a bit I tried about Orange Julius.

In a recent development, I'd love to know exactly what he was planning to say about Orange Julius, because that's another restaurant chain that feels tailor-made for a Mulaney routine. The Yoshinoya detail actually sent me down a bit of a rabbit hole because this isn't the first time the restaurant has figured into one of Mulaney's jokes.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Of course, Hader has a long history of losing it during Stefon appearances, and his inability to keep a straight face has produced some of SNL's funniest unplanned moments.

It's such an oddly specific thing to say that I can understand why Hader couldn't keep a straight face. Mulaney has a knack for finding humor in names and places that most of us probably wouldn't think twice about.

In a recent development, mulaney has certainly had plenty of success with the jokes that survived that process. Between his stand-up specials, his work on SNL and his surprisingly personal Netflix series Everybody's Live With John Mulaney, he's established himself as one of the most recognizable comedians working today.

According to recent reports, still, I have to admit that I'd happily watch an entire special made up of the jokes that didn't make the final cut. Especially if they're accompanied by stories about exactly how they fell apart. But for now, I'll happily revisit his prior specials and Everybody's Live with my Netflix subscription.

Breaking: The Cliff Booth Movie Brings Back Two Key Characters From Once Upon A Time In Hollywood

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (838 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".
  • It has been revealed that "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher.
  • It has been revealed that part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.".

It has been revealed that "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher. But still, you had to wonder if any other familiar faces would pop up in this newly introduced mis-adventure.

It has been revealed that part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history. Thanks to the actions of Cliff, actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) is not murdered by the Manson family. How does the entertainment world and Los Angeles change by 1977, when "Cliff Booth" takes place, because of that ripple effect? Tarantino wrote the script for "Cliff Booth," and if any filmmaker is equipped to dig into the nitty-gritty of such a change in Hollywood history, down to the most obscure B-pictures and forgotten TV, it's him.

Now, the major supporting cast of "Cliff Booth" is totally different. Cliff's best friend, actor Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) — for whom Cliff worked as a stunt double and driver back in 1969 — does not appear due to DiCaprio declining a cameo appearance. The movie mentions a few times that Rick moved to Australia and is right now starring in a popular TV show there, "Dingo Dan." Tarantino has also devised some stories about what happened to Rick after that fateful August 9, 1969 night.

But a few of the fictionalized Hollywood characters return for brief cameos: Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate, Timothy Olyphant as actor James Stacy, and even Nicholas Hammond as TV director Sam Wanamaker (in a smaller role).

One of the Quentin Tarantino Easter eggs in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is a commercial for Red Apple Cigarettes, a fictional brand that appears in other Tarantino movies. The actress in the commercial is Sharon Tate, with Cliff smiling at her and likely recalling how he saved her life. "Once Upon A Time In Hollywood" cast Sharon Tate in an angelic light, down to giving her the happy ending that reality didn't. But revisiting her in greater depth, like what became of her marriage to Roman Polanski or how her acting career played out, would risk adding a dash of salt to that sweet ending.

Industry observers note that the alternate history of Sharon Tate in "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" earned obvious comparisons to Tarantino's "Inglourious Basterds," which also starred Brad Pitt (as Lieutenant Aldo Raine, leader of the Nazi-killing Basterds). In that movie, Adolf Hitler (Martin Wutke) dies at the hands of Jewish soldiers instead of by suicide. That leads into Timothy Olyphant's "Cliff Booth" cameo, which feels self-recursively inspired by "Basterds.".

"Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" mixes real Hollywood history with pastiche. Much of the first half sees Dalton filming a guest spot on a TV Western, "Lancer," which was a real show back in the late '60s. Olyphant appears as the real-life star of "Lancer," James Stacy, and the episode is directed by Nicholas Hammond's Sam Wanamaker, the real director of the "Lancer" pilot episode. "Cliff Booth" gives us another glimpse of Stacy and Wanamaker working in this alternate timeline's television industry.

Industry observers note that since 1969, Cliff Booth has become a fixer: someone who (violently) solves problems for Hollywood fixtures wrapped up with criminals. Fictional TV star Charlie Winters (Scott Caan) becomes one of his clients. The movie includes a newsreel style montage, narrated by Quentin Tarantino himself, recounting Winters' rise to TV stardom.

One of Winters' indicates is "Enemy Territory," about a U.S. pilot trapped behind enemy lines in Europe during World War 2. The narrator describes the show as "'The Fugitive' with Nazis, but 'The Fugitive' with Nazis is a fun idea." (I'd watch it!) We see Winters shooting a scene where his character threatens a Gestapo officer into helping him rescue a captured American general. The officer is played by none other than Timothy-Olyphant-as-James-Stacy, doing a broad German accent with a high pitch reminiscent of Christoph Waltz's Colonel Hans Landa from "Inglourious Basterds.".

Sam Wanamaker is directing the scene. Stacy's performance is being criticized as "a smidge cavalier" — so Winters puts a live round in the prop gun with which his character is threatening the Gestapo officer. Stacy, sure enough, begins acting like a man whose life is being balanced on the edge of a trigger.

Casting Olyphant as James Stacy was a nod to how his real most famous roles are on Western TV shows — namely, Sheriff Seth Bullock in HBO's "Deadwood" and Deputy U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens in the Kentucky-set neo-Western "Justified." But Olyphant has got range beyond playing cowboys, and his comic energy in his "Cliff Booth" cameo is just more evidence of that.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is playing in theaters, with a Netflix release date of December 23, 2026.

#144169. The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1533 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Polygon ↗ Open Full Page

The 14 Best Star Wars Games of All Time, Ranked

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982.
  • Play it on: PlayStation 4, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.
  • People like Star Wars for different reasons, from the hero’s journey, to the beautiful planet environments and the thrilling space battles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium, encompassing everything from role-playing games and first-person shooters to arcade racers and XCOM clones (the latter of two seeing well-regard releases just this year). No matter the year or the hardware, some of the best Star Wars games are worth revisiting. Here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time, ranked.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

People like Star Wars for different reasons, from the hero’s journey, to the beautiful planet environments and the thrilling space battles. A lot of the best Star Wars games tend to narrow their scope rather than focusing on everything at once, and Squadrons definitely prioritized at shootouts in the vast reaches of space. It dropped players in cockpits that might have featured in the original movies and let players feel like they were in the middle of an operation… especially when they had a VR headset equipped. The online component was initially another compelling reason to play, but activity levels have dropped off in the years since launch. Still, it has a lot to offer if you don’t mind a more solitary experience.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

Respawn Entertainment has had multiple chances to do Star Wars justice, starting with this first entry in the Star Wars Jedi series. It introduces Cal Kestis, a hero living through the dark period following Revenge of the Sith. Not everyone loves the Jedi, even at the best of times. They feel a bit like the galaxy’s superheroes, and yet there’s no denying the thrill of a good lightsaber duel. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order focuses on that aspect in particular, and lets players explore interesting environments other games only allow them to glimpse from afar. It’s pretty and fun, despite performance issues at launch and some tedious backtracking.

Play it on: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X.

In a recent development, if you’re going to build a strategy game to entertain audiences in a post-XCOM world, you can do a lot worse for inspiration. Star Wars Zero Tech giant took some winning elements from that venerated franchise and transported them to a galaxy far, far away. The result is one of the greatest Star Wars games ever created, featuring compelling turn-based combat and a generally satisfying plot centered in the Clone Wars era. Some players felt the exploration segments between battles introduced unwelcome filler. And the battles themselves sometimes were a little too easy to maintain tension. But such faults, as well as technical issues at launch that included camera issues and performance drops, were minor blemishes on an otherwise standout experience that leaves us hoping for a similarly spectacular sequel.

Play it on: PlayStation 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox.

In a recent development, following closely after Star Wars: Starfighter, which released one year prior, Star Wars: Jedi Starfighter added Force abilities that proved devastating in space battles. The arsenal of weapons expanded, plus a full split-screen cooperative campaign added a newly introduced dimension to the experience. Critics at the time weren’t impressed by how much of the experience felt like the previous game, though, and the disjointed storyline couldn’t match what came before it. Even so, it served as a worthy follow-up and was better than its predecessor in some key ways. Jedi Starfighter is easy to play on a PlayStation 4, as well, despite the date of its original release.

In a recent development, when word first arrived that BioWare was working on another Star Wars RPG set in the Old Republic, visions of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic danced in our heads. However, we eventually learned that Star Wars: The Old Republic would actually take the form of an MMORPG, which dulled some of that early enthusiasm. Fortunately, the game turned out much better than it easily might have, even if it did sometimes feel like World of Warcraft in disguise and initially lacked a meaningful endgame. When early subscription numbers faltered, Electronic Arts explored a free-to-play model, allowing it to build the following it needed to justify continued development. Since then, the game has seen additional content drops, even after Disney’s acquisition of Lucasfilm. If you are so inclined, you can experience much of that content for free, thanks to the ongoing stewardship of Broadsword Online Games.

Play it on: Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

It has been revealed that lego Star Wars was a surprise hit when it arrived for PlayStation 2. A variety of sequels since then have also proven to be great fun. The Skywalker Saga is the biggest release of the lot, presenting a fresh take on the stories in all nine movies about the Skywalker family and their friends. Rather than compiling and touching up everything that came before (which is partly contained in Lego Star Wars: The Complete Saga), it presents the classic stories with a thoroughly modern touch. Some of the older elements, like a fixed camera and confusing level progression, have been cleaned up for the 2022 release. The much larger and more complex level hubs are also a satisfying development. Such improvements make The Skywalker Saga the definitive way to see your favorite Star Wars heroes doing heroic things in plastic brick form. The game is also a terrific option if you’re looking for something you can play with your less experienced friends or even small children, as one might expect from the Lego games, though the second player sometimes must take a back seat while the main hero does the tricky stuff.

A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Play it on: Nintendo 64, Windows PC.

Sources indicate that when Star Wars: Rogue Squadron debuted on the Nintendo 64, you had to buy the hardware’s mostly optional “expansion pak” to play it as the development team at Factor 5 intended. That’s how you knew you were getting something good. The added RAM brought various locations from around the Star Wars universe to life, filling them with enemy turrets and walkers that were prime targets for your lasers and rockets. The addictive gameplay loop kept college guys like me playing well into the early morning hours… and I certainly wasn’t alone. Today, the visuals are dated, but the stages still bring those memories roaring back. It’s enough to make a person want to download the Steam version and play it all over again.

Play it on: PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, Xbox Series X.

The second Star Wars Jedi game from Respawn Entertainment offered more of what we loved about the first one: numerous approaches to lightsaber combat, more open and expansive maps, and a welcome fast-travel mechanic. The story lingered near the starting line a bit longer than it should have, and some of the bosses ratcheted up the difficulty a bit unevenly. Technical issues held the experience back near launch, as well. But patches have smoothed away most of the rough edges, allowing Star Wars Jedi: Survivor to become the first-rate adventure it always deserved to be.

Play it on: PlayStation 2, PSP, Windows PC, Xbox.

Star Wars: Battlefront 2 and its predecessor are sufficiently beloved that years later, a separate developer brought them back for another go around. The original 2005 release is the one we remember most fondly, however. It let players loose on massive maps, where they could roam on foot or commandeer powerful vehicles with their friends and wreak havoc on their enemies. Although there wasn’t a lot of the depth and customization we expect from more modern shooters, the barely controlled mayhem made up for it, turning players into the architects of numerous memorable moments in one battle after another. It was arcade fun at its best, an experience the 2017 edition couldn’t quite replicate, whatever its strengths.

Play it on: PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox Series X.

In classic games like Burnout and F-Zero X, players became involved in spectacular crashes, amidst high-speed races through simple but spectacular terrain. One might say the same thing of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, our pick for the best arcade racing game in a generation. It brings a similar philosophy to the classics that came before it but applies it to landspeeders, pod racers, and speeder bikes. The game’s biggest innovation might be the lack of restarts mid-race, which raises the stakes as you careen around every sharp corner and fight for every burst of speed along the straightaways. Each upcoming vehicle you master requires different skills and comes with its own quirks, which adds variety to the experience. Venues come from a limited number of planets, which can feel repetitive over time. The plot that provides an excuse to do all that racing sometimes feels shallow, as well. But where single-player racers are concerned, they don’t get much better than this one.

Even though we just noted goodbye to him, new showrunner Victor Teran told CinemaBlend about the possibility of Pascal popping up at 51 again. He told me "anything's possible" and elaborated on that, telling CinemaBlend the connection with Severide could indicate more down the line.

I think we are always on the lookout for interesting storylines for our characters who've left the show. So we'll definitely stay on the lookout for a place. I think because of the way he mentored and guided Severide into this chair and really allowed it to happen in some ways. He'll always remain a critical part of that. And so I think it's very possible that he could emerge down the road, but he's also got a career in Phoenix for himself that he's off to.

Unlike a lot of characters on TV who get killed off, Chicago Fire included, Pascal's story was left open. He left 51 in Kelly’s hands and, as Teran pointed out, is now building his career in Arizona. That remarked, he became close with the firehouse and obviously made a mark in a short amount of time, and made sure that Kelly was ready to take over. I would love nothing more than to see Pascal again, and I could not be happier to hear Teran's response. Since Mulroney was not happy about the exit, he probably wouldn't be opposed to coming back.

Industry observers note that despite Chicago Fire’s revolving door of stars, the series has brought back a handful of former cast members from time to time. Since the show doesn’t seem to have any end in sight, it’s entirely possible that we’ll be seeing Pascal again, and not just because of what Teran told me. Chicago Fire always seems to bring back characters when you least expect it, so you never know what could happen. They just need to find a reason for him to be back in the Windy City.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Chicago Fire has been turning up the heat in Season 15. There are a handful of newbies who joined Fire as firefighter candidates. Even though it’s been fun to see Stella in more of a leadership role, it’s also been hard. One newbie got some bad news and was let go from the CFD, and I’m worried it could bring some consequences for Stella and Kelly. It's been exciting beyond characters just leaving the show.

Recent findings suggest that right now, Chicago Fire is on a brief hiatus for Thanksgiving, but the series will be back on December 9 for the fall finale, and there will certainly be some action to watch out for that Wednesday.
