9 Best Animated Witch Movies, Ranked

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Witches have been some of animation's most fascinating characters for decades, appearing as everything from terrifying supernatural villains to mischievous outsiders and young women discovering their magical abilities.
  • In a recent development, some animated witches are defined by their extraordinary powers, while others are much more interesting because of their personalities, insecurities, and relationships with the people around them.
  • In a recent development, european fairy tales, British children's literature, and North American television specials have all contributed memorable interpretations of the supernatural figure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Witches have been some of animation's most fascinating characters for decades, appearing as everything from terrifying supernatural villains to mischievous outsiders and young women discovering their magical abilities. The medium is particularly well suited to witchcraft, allowing filmmakers to bring impossible spells, enchanted forests, flying broomsticks, and elaborate magical realms to life without the limitations of live-action effects.

In a recent development, some animated witches are defined by their extraordinary powers, while others are much more interesting because of their personalities, insecurities, and relationships with the people around them. Japanese animation has produced some of the genre's most celebrated examples, particularly through the work of Studio Ghibli, but the appeal of animated witchcraft extends well beyond anime.

In a recent development, european fairy tales, British children's literature, and North American television specials have all contributed memorable interpretations of the supernatural figure. In order to keep this list focused, only movies where a witch is the protagonist or appears for a large part of the narrative are included.

Little Witch Academia is a 25-minute short film with an inventive approach to magical-school storytelling. The film introduces Atsuko "Akko" Kagari, an ordinary girl who enrolls at Luna Nova Magical Academy after being inspired by a celebrated witch named Shiny Chariot.

It has been revealed that akko's enthusiasm is considerably greater than her magical ability, which makes her a refreshing alternative to the usual effortlessly gifted fantasy protagonist. Her friendship with the more capable Lotte and Sucy provides plenty of comedy, while her determination to prove herself eventually leads to a spectacular confrontation involving a rampaging dragon.

Little Witch Academia’s animation is the real attraction, with exaggerated character expressions, energetic spell-casting, and beautifully choreographed action. Its success inspired a Kickstarter-funded sequel, The Enchanted Parade, and eventually a television series. Its short running time prevents it from reaching the emotional depth of the higher-ranked entries, but it's an exceptionally entertaining introduction to Akko's magical world.

Recent findings suggest that gilda Radner gives a wonderfully eccentric vocal performance as the titular witch in this Canadian animated Halloween special. Originally broadcast in 1978, Witch's Night Out follows a witch who wants to attend a Halloween party at her haunted mansion. When two children, Small and Tender, ask her to use magic to transform them into monsters, creating considerable chaos.

Radner's comic timing gives the witch a mischievous personality that distinguishes her from the more threatening enchantresses found in traditional fairy tales. While the film's loose, sketchy animation gives the whole production a distinctive handmade quality.

Recent findings suggest that at just 25 minutes, Witch's Night Out is a relatively modest production, but its offbeat humor, memorable character designs, and wonderfully dated disco soundtrack make it an enduring Halloween favorite. It also deserves recognition for giving children an animated witch who is more interested in having fun than frightening anybody.

In a recent development, based on Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler's beloved picture book, Room on the Broom is one of the most charming animated witch stories ever produced. It depicts a friendly witch who repeatedly stops her broomstick journey to accommodate animals who have helped her recover various lost belongings.

Gillian Anderson voices the witch, with Timothy Spall, Simon Pegg, Rob Brydon, and Sally Hawkins among the supporting cast. The film's greatest strength is its simple understanding of kindness and cooperation, with the witch's generosity eventually becoming the very thing that saves her when a dragon threatens to eat her.

The adaptation also makes excellent use of the original book's illustrations, translating Scheffler's distinctive character designs into expressive computer animation. Its Oscar nomination for Best Animated Short Film and BAFTA Children's Award win were thoroughly deserved. Room on the Broom may be aimed primarily at younger viewers, but its warmth and visual charm make it an absolute delight.

According to recent reports, this charming Czechoslovak and West German animated fantasy deserves considerably more international recognition. Based on Otfried Preußler's children's book, The Little Witch follows a young enchantress who desperately wants to attend the witches' annual gathering on Walpurgis Night. Unfortunately, she's considered too young by the other witches, who give her a year to prove herself worthy of joining them.

Accompanied by her raven Abraxas, the Little Witch sets about learning how to become a good witch. However, her unconventional understanding of witchcraft eventually brings her into conflict with the established magical authorities.

According to recent reports, the distinctive animation gives The Little Witch a wonderfully folkloric atmosphere, while its central character offers an appealing alternative to the traditional wicked witch. Rather than celebrating magical power for its own sake, the story considers what makes somebody good and whether authority deserves unquestioning obedience. Though hampered by its limited budget, the combination of European folklore, gentle humor, and rebellious spirit makes it one of the most interesting entries here.

Walt Disney Animation Studios returns to witchcraft with Hexed, an original magical coming-of-age adventure featuring Hailee Steinfeld as Billie Doe. An unconventional teenager who has never quite fitted in, Billie discovers that she possesses extraordinary magical abilities, transporting herself from suburban life into the fantastical witch realm of Hexe.

The supporting voice cast is particularly impressive, including Jodie Foster as the sinister Queen Celeste, Walton Goggins as a magical three-eyed cat, and Stephen Fry as an enchanted journal.

Sources indicate that hexed has an appealing mother-daughter relationship at its center, giving its magical adventure an emotional dimension beyond the usual discovery-of-powers storyline. Its elaborate fantasy setting and colorful supernatural characters also make it a particularly exciting addition to Disney's animated catalog. It hasn't yet had the time to establish the legacy of the classics above it, but its premise and creative ambition earn it a place among the genre's most promising modern entries.

Studio Ponoc's first feature film has plenty of the magical wonder associated with its creators' previous work at Studio Ghibli. Based on Mary Stewart's 1971 novel The Little Broomstick, Mary And The Witch's Flower follows Mary Smith, a young girl who discovers a mysterious flower that blooms once every seven years. Its magical properties temporarily grant her extraordinary abilities, allowing her to fly on a broomstick and gain admission to the mysterious Endor College.

Director Hiromasa Yonebayashi previously worked on Spirited Away and directed The Secret World of Arrietty and When Marnie Was There. His experience is evident in the film's gorgeous environments, expressive character animation, and imaginative magical sequences.

Its story occasionally relies on familiar fantasy conventions, and at times can feel quite narratively thin. However, Mary and the Witch's Flower captures the excitement of discovering a world where almost anything is possible through utterly entrancing visuals.

Belladonna of Sadness is easily the most adult and disturbing film on this list. The experimental Japanese animation follows Jeanne, a peasant woman who turns to the Devil after suffering horrific abuse at the hands of her feudal lord. Her supernatural bargain gradually transforms her into a powerful witch, but her growing influence threatens the patriarchal authorities who control the community.

As Jeanne gains confidence and power, the film develops into a provocative exploration of female sexuality, oppression, and rebellion. Visually, Belladonna of Sadness is unlike almost anything else in animation. Its watercolor imagery, elaborate compositions, and psychedelic sequences frequently resemble moving illustrations rather than conventional cartoons.

Sources indicate that much of Belladonna Of Sadness uses limited animation, allowing its artwork to carry the emotional weight of the story. The sexual violence and explicit imagery make it emphatically unsuitable for younger audiences, but its audacious artistic direction and unconventional feminist themes make it one of the most enchanting animated witch films ever produced.

According to recent reports, spirited Away is rightly considered one of the greatest animated films ever made, and its central antagonist is one of animation's most memorable witches. When ten-year-old Chihiro becomes trapped in the spirit world, she must find work at a gigantic bathhouse operated by Yubaba, a formidable sorceress who steals her employees' names and exercises extraordinary control over their lives.

Yubaba is a brilliant creation. Her enormous head, extravagant appearance, and terrifying magical abilities make her immediately imposing. The film's witchcraft is also woven into its wider exploration of Japanese folklore, with Yubaba's bathhouse populated by spirits, strange creatures, and supernatural visitors. Chihiro's survival does not depend on learning magical abilities, but rather developing courage, compassion, and resourcefulness.

According to recent reports, winner of the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature, Spirited Away is a truly extraordinary achievement in storytelling and animation. Yubaba alone makes it essential viewing for anyone interested in animated witches, even if the film's brilliance extends far beyond its supernatural antagonist.

According to recent reports, hayao Miyazaki's Kiki's Delivery Service is the definitive animated witch movie because it understands that magic is often most interesting when examining everyday life. Based on Eiko Kadono's novel, it depicts 13-year-old Kiki, who leaves home with her talking black cat Jiji to complete a traditional year of independent living.

With flying as her only magical skill, she establishes an aerial delivery service from a local bakery, gradually building friendships and discovering the responsibilities of adulthood. However, her magical abilities aren't unlimited, and the pressures of independence eventually cause her to lose her ability to fly.

Rather than relying on a conventional villain or world-threatening magical crisis, Kiki's Delivery Service is built around a relatable experience of adolescence: losing confidence in something that once came naturally. The animation is beautiful, particularly the detailed European-inspired city and the expressive sequences of Kiki flying above its rooftops. Other animated films might feature more powerful witches or more elaborate displays of magic, but few capture the wonder of being a young witch quite as convincingly as Kiki's Delivery Service.

In a recent development, if you’re not the type to share karaoke videos online, another nice iOS 27.3 change is that the lyrics view for songs has gotten an iPhone Duo-inspired upgrade in landscape mode. Now, artwork for the song you’re listening to blends beautifully into the stream of lyrics.

Apple Fitness+ is getting a big expansion in iOS 27.3 with a fresh Gym Strength program.

Gym Strength lets you build a strength program that fits your schedule and the equipment you have on hand. It’s fully customizable and provides Apple’s best offering yet for traditional strength training.

Whether you’re brand newly introduced to strength training or just benefit from some additional structure, Gym Strength is a great reason to try out Fitness+.

Recent findings suggest that apple’s Freeform app gets a handful of improvements in iOS 27.3, including fresh text styling options and preset background colors to choose from. You can also generate custom shapes using Apple Intelligence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are not only my favorite earbuds I've ever owned, they might also be my favorite headphones of all time. The Pros sound great, come with excellent noise cancellation and transparency modes, and are packed with modern features that go beyond listening to music. I'd recommend these to any Apple user looking for the best overall audio experience at full price, but when they're $100 off, I actively encourage you to buy these now.

On the surface, Apple's third-generation AirPods Pro are among the best ways to listen to audio on your Apple devices. The earbuds sound great: I'm not an audiophile or a headphone reviewer, but to my ears, the Pros deliver excellent sound quality, with plenty of bass and great sound separation. I frequently turn to mine when I want to pay close attention to a new album, or watch a show or movie with intricate sound design. Plus, like other AirPods, the Pros are great for jumping between your various Apple devices. I'm constantly switching between my iPhone, Mac, and Apple TV with mine, and they seamlessly move between each—at least, most of the time.

Industry observers note that the noise cancellation on these AirPods is also stellar. I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

Industry observers note that there are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

According to recent reports, this isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

Samsung’s 65-inch S90H is down to $1,397.99 from $1,897.99, saving you $500 on the organization’s mid-range OLED TV for 2026. It has been revealed that one of the biggest discounts in this roundup, the 2026 75-inch Hisense U7 is now $997.99, down from $1,999.99. Gaming-focused features also make it worth a look if you plan to connect a current-generation console or gaming PC.

According to recent reports, for a more affordable 75-inch option, Hisense's 2026 U6 Pro is down to $699.99 from $1,399.99, saving you $700. The C6 is LG’s mid-range OLED evo model for 2026, and right now its 65-inch model is $1,399.99, down from its $2,699.99 launch price. According to recent reports, sony’s 65-inch Bravia 6, the entry-level OLED in its 2026 TV lineup, is now $1,198, down from $1,999.99, saving you $802. In a recent development, that depends on your budget, room size, and how you plan to use it. The LG OLED evo C6 and Samsung S90H are worth considering for movie enthusiasts and gamers who want excellent contrast and smooth motion, while the Hisense U7 and TCL QM64L offer mini-LED alternatives for brighter living rooms. For a large screen at a relatively affordable price, the 75-inch Hisense U6 Pro at $699.99 stands out, while the 65-inch Roku Plus Series at $449.99 makes sense for everyday streaming on a tighter budget. If screen size is your priority, the 98-inch TCL F8D is also worth a look, provided you have the room for it.

It has been revealed that choosing between OLED and QLED is an crucial decision you need to ask yourself before you go shopping for TVs. If you can afford an OLED and want the best image possible, go for the OLED. Just make sure you're okay with the dimmer lights they emit. If you need brightness and don't want to blow out your budget on a TV, go with a QLED.

  • Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I've read more than 30 books in the past year, all of them on an e-reader with a screen roughly the size of a credit card. If you think that sounds untenable, I say: Don't knock it 'til you've tried it. Once you're immersed in a book, you'll find the size doesn't matter, and the convenience of being able to slip it into any pocket and forget it's there means you need never be without it.

Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. This is the cheapest e-reader with a light and a touchscreen that you can buy right now, and it's well worth the money.

It has been revealed that the X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two big upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

As much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Apple is wrapping up a packed year for new products, but there are already several 2027 launches I’m very excited for. Here are my current most anticipated new products rumored for next year.

The iPhone’s 20th anniversary is rumored to bring a special newly introduced model that’s been dubbed ‘iPhone 20 Pro.’.

iPhone 20 Pro is expected to introduce a upcoming design inspired by the iPhone Air, reintroducing curves and possibly titanium, and with a quad-curved display that wraps around the edges for a bezel-free appearance.

According to recent reports, I recently decided the iPhone Duo wasn’t the right model for me. While I’ll certainly be interested to see how the device evolves in its second generation, I’m far more excited for the iPhone 20 Pro as a fresh iteration on slab phones. Combining the strengths of a Pro model (cameras, battery) with the design traits of iPhone Air sounds very compelling.

I’ve been using Apple’s HomeView a lot since getting one earlier this month. And despite some Siri hiccups likely tied to the iOS 27.3 beta, I’m overall really loving the product and my family is too.

Because HomeView has been a hit for us, I’m eager to see how Apple evolves and expands it with the rumored ‘HomeView Ultra’ with a 9-inch screen that can automatically rotate 360° to face whoever’s speaking.

I have no complaints about the current HomeView’s size, but am intrigued by a larger screen’s impact on the overall experience. Mostly though, the idea of a HomeView that automatically rotates to face you sounds really useful. There’s a spot in my kitchen that would be perfect for kitchen and dining room use if the screen could swivel automatically.

The Apple Watch Series 13 might introduce an overhauled design, with one leaker claiming it will break compatibility of watch bands.

I’m tempering my expectations for this, since plenty of Apple Watch redesign rumors have come and gone with little actual change. But Mark Gurman has hinted we might get a redesigned Watch next year too. And after years of the same basic look, I’m fascinated to see what the next generation of Apple Watch design could be.

It has been revealed that I’m very happy with my Apple Watch Series 12, and it’s becoming even more powerful with watchOS 27.3. But it’s very much an update focused on internals, so if Apple does deliver an external overhaul, the newly introduced Watch will merit its spot among my most anticipated products list.

It has been revealed that getting your gaming gear fix during the holiday shopping season is an annual tradition, but it’s more crucial this year than ever. The RAM shortage has driven up all electronics prices, right when the biggest game of all time arrives after a 13-year wait. So any discount you can score can have a big impact on your wallet. Before the main event starts, you can get started with some early Black Friday gaming deals here.

Game consoles are obviously more expensive than they used to be, even when they came out years ago. But bundle deals are still some of the best way to shave some cash off the sticker price. We’ve also got some deals on accessories, which aren’t always hit quite as hard by the component shortage, so there’s more room for savings.

Sources indicate that well, let’s get the bad news out of the way up front: There probably won’t be that many deals on console hardware. Certain retailers might offer discounts on bundles, but given the price increases over the last year, and the already-high demand, your best bet for those is likely checking individual retailers close to you.

Nintendo’s the only major outlier, with a discounted Switch 2 with Mario Kart World bundle for $500, or $50 off the normal retail price. That deal will be live now through Dec. 5. You can also pick up a Switch 2 bundle with Switch Sports Resort for $530. If you’re still interested in VR, you can also pick up a Meta Quest 3S bundle for $298 ($52 off) through Saturday.

PC gaming is just as susceptible to the component shortage as consoles, but since there’s a wider range of models, it’s a bit easier to find deals on individual units.

It, of course, has a heart rate sensor to keep tabs on your pulse, including high and low heart rate alerts; the ability to track dozens of different workouts and exercise types (including swimming, thanks to the device's water resistance); a sleep tracker with daily analyses available in the Health app; notification forwarding to check in on your alerts without opening your iPhone; and the ability to send and receive text messages.

It comes in two sizes (40mm and 44mm) depending on how large or small you prefer your watch. No matter which model you get, the watch comes with the S10 chip, Apple's last-generation watch processor. While it isn't as fast as the current S11 chip, the S10 is more than capable of running watchOS 27. Apple states the SE 3 can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge, and up to 32 hours in Low Power Mode, with fast charging from 0% to 80% in 45 minutes.

Industry observers note that the majority of the features missing from the SE 3 aren't essential. Apple's other watches have things like bigger, brighter displays, additional health tracking tools like hypertension alerts and an ECG sensor, longer battery life, and Audio Intelligence—the latter of which might be a benefit to miss, depending on who you are.

Sources indicate that if your giftee wants or needs any of those additional features, Series 12 or Ultra 4 might be a better choice. But for anyone who wants the essential Apple Watch experience, the SE 3 is simply the best-value watch Apple sells right now—especially at this discount. Right now, the watch starts at $199 for the 40mm watch, or $229 for the 44mm. You can also save on the cellular versions of these watches: $249 for the cellular 40mm watch, and $279 for the cellular 44mm model.

iOS 27 gave your iPhone an alarm feature that’s long been missing

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (391 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alarms are one of the most important iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a latest volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.
  • Have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm?
  • I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alarms are one of the most important iPhone features, and iOS 27 offers a key feature that should help your alarm actually wake you: a latest volume setting for alarms that’s independent of other volume settings.

Have you ever accidentally slept through an alarm? We’ve all done it. And most often for me, it’s because my alarm volume was unintentionally set to a very low level.

I suspect that’s a pretty common reason for missed alarms. And in iOS 27, Apple finally has the fix—but it requires manually setting up.

Inside Settings ⇾ Sounds & Haptics, you can now set a volume for alarms that’s independent from the systemwide ringtone setting.

It has been revealed that iOS 27 has two new sections in this Settings screen: Alarms and Timers, and Alerts and System Sounds. Both include ‘Match Ringtone Volume’ toggles that are on by default. This means your volume for alarms, timers, alerts, and other system sounds are all determined by the ringtone volume.

But if you disable the Alarms and Timers toggle, you’ll get a new volume slider that applies only to those system functions, and won’t be impacted by your ringtone volume.

As seen above, this means you can crank the Alarms and Timers volume up to the maximum level without making every other system sound, including notifications and phone calls, be similarly deafening.

So the next time you sleep through your alarm, it won’t be because the alarm was too quiet.

In case you missed it, iOS 26 introduced a welcome feature that lets you set custom snooze durations for alarms, and also an option to have alarms trigger on your iPhone even if you’re wearing an Apple Watch.

Sources indicate that do you initiative to set a custom volume setting for alarms in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

Tech Report: MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat.
  • MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.
  • It has been revealed that heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the biggest glitch with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

It has been revealed that heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker states it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

According to recent reports, the result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

The single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker notes that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Industry observers note that anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

According to recent reports, there’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also quickly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I said in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

Breaking: 1Password Security Incident

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (718 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Update: We will be providing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with details in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete.
  • In a recent development, on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • Industry observers note that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update: We will be providing a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) with details in the coming weeks once our full investigation is complete.

In a recent development, on November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

Industry observers note that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

Recent findings suggest that the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of owners in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added latest detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

Recent findings suggest that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a new device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

We are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll update it if we find anything that changes what we’ve noted here.

#144020. Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to significant issues.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer says it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to significant issues.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he claims he has identified the next significant shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

In a recent development, ng’s current efforts are focused on his company Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he says can yield “small data” solutions to big issues in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

The great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Andrew Ng: This is a big question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a new paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

In a recent development, ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

It has been revealed that having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of users, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of owners.

In a recent development, ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from substantial data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and said, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Industry observers note that over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing newly introduced here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

In a recent development, ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

The data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one firm or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that showed up.

Industry observers note that you often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

In a recent development, ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

Sources indicate that when you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand fresh model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Industry observers note that ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having noted that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For massive data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

For example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very promptly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

In a recent development, could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

Recent findings suggest that ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Upcoming tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an crucial piece of the puzzle.

Industry observers note that one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

Ng: In AI, data cleaning is crucial, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention rapidly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

For example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

Ng: I think synthetic data is an key tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

Recent findings suggest that “In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion consumers. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

According to recent reports, synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

Industry observers note that to make these concerns more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a company approaches Landing AI and states it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

It has been revealed that ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

One of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

In a recent development, ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and enhancement the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion owners. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent new neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s key for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

In a recent development, ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print glitch as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the announcement yesterday that the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed due to weather, the event’s co-host Hoda Kotb stopped by Late Night to express her relief that it has been rescheduled for Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that “The people who have been preparing this 100-year parade have been working tirelessly for a year-plus,” Kotb told host Seth Meyers. “The musical acts are incredible. So imagine spending all that time painting every little bit of every float, wondering if the float is going to fly away somewhere. So the good news is, to me, I’m relieved. Saturday is going to be amazing. Everybody’s still hanging out. We’re going to watch it anyway.”.

It has been revealed that she added, “It’s going to be literally out of this world. It’s amazing.”.

Weather experts have been warning U.S. residents about a rapidly approaching storm system making its way up the east coast, bringing with it high winds, heavy rains, and flood warnings. According to CNN, winds in New York City are expected to reach around 25 to 35 mph today — which would be dangerous for the parade’s famous floats and giant balloons.

“The safety of our participants and spectators is our top priority, and after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” Macy’s noted in a statement. “Thank you to the thousands of volunteers, performers and partners who create the magic millions enjoy each year. We look forward to celebrating together on Saturday.” Trending Stories Duran Duran Guitarist Andy Taylor Dead at 65 U2 Perform Dolly Parton's Final Recording During NFL Halftime Show ⁠Gérard Depardieu to Face Trial for Allegedly Raping Actress Charlotte ⁠Arnould Duran Duran’s Andy Taylor Was the Wildest of the Wild Boys.

This is the first time the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade has been postponed because of inclimate weather. It was cancelled in 1942, 1943, and 1944 because the U.S. needed all excess helium and rubber for the World War II effort.

Sources indicate that kotb is set to co-host the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade alongside Savannah Guthrie and Al Roker. Grammy-nominated singer Raye is expected to open the parade with a holiday performance featuring her sisters, Amma and Absolutely; followed by floats and performances by Wyclef Jean, Smash Mouth, Natasha Bedingfield, Icona Pop, JoJo, Hunger Games star McKenna Grace, and Queen Latifah. No additional changes to the parade programming or lineup have been announced.

Patch, November 23: The Citrus MacBook Neo with 256GB of storage has dropped even further. It’s now $100 off, sitting at $599. This one will probably sell out fast, so don’t wait! The rest of the MacBook Neo lineup is still $50 off.

It has been revealed that the most affordable current-generation MacBook you can get under the tree this year just dropped to its best prices in several months with today’s extremely rare early Black Friday deals. Apple’s MacBook Neo lineup is nearly $50 off to deliver one of, if not the most surprising discounts of the 2026 Black Friday season yet.

Amazon has decided to get even more aggressive with its early Black Friday offerings this week with a solid discount on Apple’s 2026 MacBook Neo, right after delivering AirPods Pro 3 down at an impressive $70 off and the best prices ever across the Apple Watch Series 12 lineup.

As part of the giant collection of upcoming deals landing in its Black Friday sale section this week, it has now dropped the 256GB MacBook Neo down to $649.99 shipped, while the elevated 512GB model sporting the Touch ID keyboard down to $749.99 shipped. Both models are available in various color options at the discounted rate.

While we aren’t talking about something like the major $250 price drops live on the M5 MacBook Air lineup right now, this is, after all, the already extremely affordable current-generation MacBook, at least by Apple standards and despite this summer’s price increase.

While there was a time when you could score one of these for less in brand fresh condition at retail, those days are long gone now with no signs of return. MacBook Neo remains the most affordable way to land your special someone, or yourself, a new current MacBook this holiday, and it is now at the lowest price we have tracked since the price increases in late June.

It is also worth noting that, while they were lower at launch, there were no overly significant deals back then either and it’s not likely they will drop much lower than they are right now. Not much is safe from Black Friday these days, but the MacBook Neo could have been one of only a very small handful of Apple releases that had and still has the potential to dodge the November price slashing.

Today’s surprisingly rare discounts land on the heels of Apple official raising the eduction pricing at the tail end of last month, and the release of “The Dreamer” – Apple’s new 2026 holiday film starring the new Neo.
